translations.text: The Lord spoke with Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the Tent of Meeting, on the first day of the second month in the second year after the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt. He said to him:
Take a census of the whole congregation of the Israelites, by their clans and their ancestral households, counting the names of every male, one by one.
You and your brother Aaron are to count them by their military divisions, everyone in Israel twenty years old and above who goes out to serve in the army.
With you there is to be one man from each tribe, each a head of his ancestral household.
These are the names of the men who are to stand with you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
from the sons of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
from Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran;
from Gad, Eliasaph son of Reuel;
from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.
These were the distinguished men of the congregation, the leaders of the tribes of their ancestral households. They were the heads of the thousands of Israel.
Moses and Aaron took these men who had been designated by name.

They assembled the whole congregation on the first day of the second month. They were counted by their clans and their ancestral households, with their names counted one by one, from twenty years old and above.
As the Lord had commanded Moses, he counted them in the wilderness of Sinai.

The descendants of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn, were recorded by their lines of descent, their clans, and their ancestral households, counting the names of every male one by one, from twenty years old and above, everyone in Israel who went out to serve in the army.
The number counted from the tribe of Reuben was forty-six thousand five hundred.

The descendants of Simeon were recorded by their lines of descent, their clans, and their ancestral households, counting the names of every male one by one, from twenty years old and above, everyone in Israel who went out to serve in the army.
The number counted from the tribe of Simeon was fifty-nine thousand three hundred.

The descendants of Gad were recorded by their lines of descent, their clans, and their ancestral households, counting the names of every male one by one, from twenty years old and above, everyone in Israel who went out to serve in the army.
The number counted from the tribe of Gad was forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
And the descendants of Judah were listed by their genealogies, clans, and ancestral households, with their names counted, from twenty years old and up—all eligible for military service in Israel.
The number counted from the tribe of Judah was 74,600.
And the descendants of Issachar were listed by their genealogies, clans, and ancestral households, with their names counted, from twenty years old and up—all eligible for military service in Israel.
The number counted from the tribe of Issachar was 54,400.
And the descendants of Zebulun were listed by their genealogies, clans, and ancestral households, with their names counted, from twenty years old and up—all eligible for military service in Israel.
The number counted from the tribe of Zebulun was 57,400.

And among the descendants of Joseph, the descendants of Ephraim were listed by their genealogies, clans, and ancestral households, with their names counted, from twenty years old and up—all eligible for military service in Israel.
The number counted from the tribe of Ephraim was 40,500.
And the descendants of Manasseh were listed by their genealogies, clans, and ancestral households, with their names counted, from twenty years old and up—all eligible for military service in Israel.
The number counted from the tribe of Manasseh was 32,200.
And the descendants of Benjamin were listed by their genealogies, clans, and ancestral households, with their names counted, from twenty years old and up—all eligible for military service in Israel.
The number counted from the tribe of Benjamin was 35,400.
And the descendants of Dan were listed by their genealogies, clans, and ancestral households, with their names counted, from twenty years old and up—all eligible for military service in Israel.
The number counted from the tribe of Dan was 62,700.
And the descendants of Asher were listed by their genealogies, clans, and ancestral households, with their names counted, from twenty years old and up—all eligible for military service in Israel.
The number counted from the tribe of Asher was 41,500.
And the descendants of Naphtali were listed by their genealogies, clans, and ancestral households, with their names counted, from twenty years old and up—all eligible for military service in Israel.
The number counted from the tribe of Naphtali was 53,400.
These were those counted by Moses and Aaron and the leaders of Israel, twelve men, each representing his ancestral household.
And all the Israelites counted by their ancestral households were from twenty years old and up—all eligible for military service in Israel.
And the total number of Israelites counted was 603,550.
But the Levites, according to their ancestral tribe, were not counted among them.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Do not count the tribe of Levi or include their number among the Israelites.

Instead, put the Levites in charge of the tabernacle of the testimony, all its utensils, and everything in it. They are to carry the tabernacle and all its utensils, and they are to serve it and camp around the tabernacle.”
When the tabernacle sets out, the Levites shall take it down, and when the tabernacle comes to rest, the Levites shall set it up. Any outsider who approaches it shall be put to death.
The Israelites shall camp, each in his own camp and each under his own standard, according to their divisions.
The Levites shall camp around the tabernacle of the testimony, so that wrath may not fall upon the congregation of the Israelites. The Levites shall keep watch over the tabernacle of the testimony.
The Israelites did just as the Lord commanded Moses; that is what they did.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
The Israelites shall camp, each under his own standard, in the places assigned to their ancestral households. They shall camp facing the tent of meeting, all around it.
Those camping at the front, on the east, shall be under the standard of the camp of Judah, according to their divisions. The leader of the people of Judah shall be Nahshon son of Amminadab.
The number of his division is 74,600.
The tribe of Issachar shall camp beside him. The leader of the people of Issachar shall be Nethanel son of Zuar.
The number of his division is 54,400.
And the tribe of Zebulun: the leader of the people of Zebulun shall be Eliab son of Helon.
The number of his troops was fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
The total number of the camp of Judah, according to their divisions, is 186,400. They shall set out first.
The standard of the camp of Reuben shall be on the south, according to their divisions. The leader of the people of Reuben shall be Elizur son of Shedeur.
The number of his division is 46,500.
The tribe of Simeon shall camp beside him. The leader of the people of Simeon shall be Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
The number of his division is 59,300.
And the tribe of Gad: the leader of the people of Gad shall be Eliasaph son of Reuel.
The number of his division is 45,650.
The total number of the camp of Reuben, according to their divisions, is 151,450. They shall set out after the first group.

Then the tent of meeting shall set out with the camp of the Levites in the middle of the camps. They shall set out in the same order in which they camp, each with his own standard, according to their divisions.
The standard of the camp of Ephraim shall be on the west, according to their divisions. The leader of the people of Ephraim shall be Elishama son of Ammihud.
The number of his division is 40,500.
The tribe of Manasseh shall camp beside him. The leader of the people of Manasseh shall be Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
The number of his division is 32,200.
And the tribe of Benjamin: the leader of the people of Benjamin shall be Abidan son of Gideoni.
His force numbered 35,400.
The total number of troops in the camp of Ephraim was one hundred eight thousand one hundred. They shall set out after the two.
The standard of the camp of Dan is to be on the north, according to their divisions. The leader of the people of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
His force numbered 62,700.
The tribe of Asher is to camp beside him. The leader of the people of Asher is Pagiel son of Ocran.
His force numbered 41,500.
Then comes the tribe of Naphtali. The leader of the people of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan.
His force numbered 53,400.
The total number counted in the camp of Dan was 157,600. They are to set out last under their standards.
These are the Israelites who were counted according to their ancestral households. All those counted in the camps, according to their divisions, numbered 603,550.
The Levites and their ancestral tribe were not counted among the Israelites, as the Lord commanded Moses.

The Israelites did everything that the Lord commanded Moses. This is what they did: they set out under their standards and camped in this way, each in his own camp according to his ancestral household.
These are the descendants of Aaron and Moses at the time when the Lord spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
These are the names of Aaron’s sons: Nadab his firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron the priest, who were anointed and ordained to the priesthood.

Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai. They had no sons. Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests during the lifetime of their father Aaron.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
“Bring the tribe of Levi forward and present them before Aaron the priest, so that they may serve him.
They are to carry out his duties and the duties of the whole congregation before the Lord, in front of the Tent of Meeting, performing the service of the tabernacle.
They shall look after all the equipment of the tent of meeting and carry out the duties of the Israelites, performing the service of the tabernacle.
You shall give the Levites to Aaron and his sons. They are given to him as a gift from among the Israelites.
Appoint Aaron and his sons to guard their priesthood. Any outsider who approaches must be put to death.”
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
Look, I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the Israelites, so that the Levites shall be mine.

For every firstborn is mine. On the day when I killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to myself every firstborn of the Israelites, both human and livestock. They shall be mine. I am the Lord.
The Lord spoke with Moses in the wilderness of Sinai and said to him:
“Count the descendants of Levi according to their ancestral households and their clans. You are to count every male a month old or older.”
Moses counted them at the Lord’s spoken command, as he had been commanded.
These were the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
These are the names of the sons of Gershon according to their clans: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath, by their clans: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari, by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites according to their ancestral houses.
To Gershon belonged the clan of Libni and the clan of Shimei. These are the clans of Gershon.
Their number, counting every male a month old and older, was seven thousand five hundred.
The clan of Gershon shall camp behind the tabernacle, on the west.
The leader of the ancestral house of Gershon was Eliasaph son of Eliab.
The sons of Gershon were responsible for these things in the tent of meeting: the tabernacle, the entrance screen and its covering, and the curtain at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Also the hangings of the courtyard, the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard surrounding the tabernacle and the altar, its ropes, and all the work connected with it.
To Kohath belonged the clan of Amram, the clan of Izhar, the clan of Hebron, and the clan of Uzziel. These are the clans of Kohath.
Their number, counting every male a month old and older, was eight thousand six hundred, who were responsible for the care of the sanctuary.
The clan of the house of Kohath shall camp along the side of the tabernacle, on the south.
The leader of the ancestral house of the clan of Kohath was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
They were responsible for the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altar, the sacred utensils used in service, the entrance screen, and all the work connected with it.
The chief of the leaders of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, who supervised those responsible for the care of the sanctuary.
To Merari belonged the clan of Mahli and the clan of Mushi. These are the clans of Merari.
Their number, counting every male a month old and older, was six thousand two hundred.
The leader of the ancestral house of the clan of Merari was Zuriel son of Abihail. They shall camp along the side of the tabernacle, on the north.
The sons of Merari were assigned responsibility for the boards of the tabernacle, its bars, its posts, its bases, all its equipment, and all the work connected with it.
Also the pillars all around the courtyard, their ropes, their bases, and their hangings.

Those camping in front of the tabernacle on the east, in front of the tent of meeting on the east, were Moses, Aaron, and his sons. They were responsible for the care of the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Any outsider who approaches shall be put to death.
The total number of Levites whom Moses counted at the LORD's command, every male a month old and older, was twenty-two thousand.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him, “Count every firstborn male among the Israelites a month old and older, and take a count of their names.
You shall present the Levites to me—I am the LORD—in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn livestock of the Israelites.”
Moses counted all the firstborn of the Israelites, as the LORD had commanded him.
All the firstborn males a month old and older, counted by name, numbered twenty-two thousand two hundred seventy-three.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
Bring forward the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites shall belong to me. I am the Lord.
As for the redemption of the two hundred and seventy-three firstborn of the Israelites who exceed the number of the Levites:
Take five shekels per person, according to the sanctuary shekel, reckoning twenty gerahs to a shekel.
Give the redemption money for those who exceed their number to Aaron and his sons.
Moses took the redemption money from those who exceeded the number redeemed by the Levites.
From the firstborn of the Israelites he took the money: one thousand three hundred and sixty-five shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons according to the word of the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
Take a census of the descendants of Kohath from among the descendants of Levi, by their clans and their ancestral households,
from thirty years old and upward to fifty years old, everyone who enters the service to do the work in the tent of meeting.
This is the service of the descendants of Kohath in the tent of meeting: the care of the most holy things.
When the camp sets out, Aaron and his sons shall go in and take down the curtain stretched across the entrance, and cover the ark of the testimony with it.
They shall spread over it a covering of skins of [?], spread a cloth entirely of blue over that, and put its carrying poles in place.
Over the table of the Presence they shall spread a blue cloth, and on it they shall put the dishes, bowls, pitchers, and vessels for pouring offerings. The bread shall remain on it continually.
They shall spread a scarlet cloth over it, cover it with a covering of skins of [?], and put its carrying poles in place.
They shall take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand for lighting, its lamps, its tongs, its trays, and all the oil vessels used in tending it.
They shall put it and all its utensils inside a covering of skins of [?], and place it on its carrying poles.
Over the golden altar they shall spread a cloth entirely of blue, cover it with a covering of skins of [?], and put its carrying poles in place.
They shall take all the utensils used for service in the sanctuary, put them in a blue cloth, cover them with a covering of skins of [?], and place them on carrying poles.
They shall clear the altar and spread a purple cloth over it.

They shall put with it all the utensils used in serving at it: the firepans, forks, shovels, basins, and all the altar’s utensils. They shall spread over it a covering of skins of [?] and put its carrying poles in place.

When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy things and all the sanctuary’s utensils, when the camp sets out, then the descendants of Kohath shall come in to carry them. They must not touch the holy things, or they will die. These are the things the descendants of Kohath must carry in the tent of meeting.

Eleazar son of Aaron the priest shall have charge of the oil for lighting, the fragrant incense, the regular flour offering, and the anointing oil. He shall oversee the whole tabernacle and everything in it, including the sanctuary and its utensils.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
Do not let the clan of Kohath be destroyed from among the Levites.
Instead, do this for them so that they may live and not die when they enter among the most holy things: Aaron and his sons shall go in and assign each man his service and what he is to carry.
They must not enter to look while the holy things are being covered, or they will die.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Take a census of the descendants of Gershon as well, by their ancestral households and their clans.
Count them from thirty years old and upward, up to fifty years old, everyone who comes to join the service and do the work at the tent of meeting.
This is the work of the clan of Gershon: serving and carrying loads.
They shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting and its entrance curtain, the covering of colored leather that lies over it, and the entrance curtain of the tent of meeting.

Also the hangings of the courtyard, the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard surrounding the tabernacle and the altar, their ropes, and all the equipment for their service—everything they use in their work and service.

All the service of the descendants of Gershon shall be under the direction of Aaron and his sons, including everything they carry and all their work. You shall assign them responsibility for everything they carry.
This is the service of the clan of the descendants of Gershon at the tent of meeting. Their responsibilities shall be under the supervision of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
You shall count the descendants of Merari by their clans and their ancestral households.
Count them from thirty years old and upward, up to fifty years old, everyone who comes to join the service and do the work at the tent of meeting.
These are the loads entrusted to them to carry as part of all their service at the tent of meeting: the boards of the tabernacle, its crossbars, its pillars, and its bases.
Also the pillars around the courtyard, their bases, their pegs, their ropes, all their equipment, and everything used in their service. List by name the articles entrusted to them to carry.
This is the service of the clan of the descendants of Merari, all their work at the tent of meeting, under the supervision of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the congregation counted the descendants of Kohath by their clans and their ancestral households,
from thirty years old and upward, up to fifty years old, everyone who entered the service to work at the tent of meeting.
The number counted by their clans was two thousand seven hundred and fifty.
These were those counted from the clan of Kohath, everyone serving at the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the Lord’s command through Moses.
And those counted from the descendants of Gershon, by their clans and their ancestral households,
from thirty years old and upward, up to fifty years old, everyone who entered the service to work at the tent of meeting.
The number counted by their clans and their ancestral households was two thousand six hundred and thirty.
These were those counted from the clan of the descendants of Gershon, everyone serving at the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the Lord’s command.
And those counted from the clan of the descendants of Merari, by their clans and their ancestral households,
from thirty years old and upward, up to fifty years old, everyone who entered the service to work at the tent of meeting.
The number counted by their clans was three thousand two hundred.
These were those counted from the clans of the descendants of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the Lord’s command through Moses.
All the Levites whom Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel counted, by their clans and their ancestral households.
From thirty years old and upward, up to fifty years old: everyone who enters the service to perform the work of ministry and the service of carrying loads in the tent of meeting.
Their total number was eight thousand five hundred and eighty.
At the LORD’s command, they were counted through Moses, each man according to his work and what he was to carry. He counted them as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Command the Israelites to send outside the camp everyone who has leprosy, everyone who has a discharge, and everyone who is unclean through contact with a dead body.
Whether male or female, you must send them outside the camp, so that they do not defile your camp, where I dwell among you.”
The Israelites did so and sent them outside the camp. Just as the LORD had told Moses, so the Israelites did.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Tell the Israelites: If a man or woman commits any of the sins people commit and acts wrongfully before the LORD, that person becomes guilty.
They must confess the sins they have committed. The offender must make full restitution for the wrong, add one-fifth to it, and return it to the person who was wronged.

If the man has no close relative to receive restitution for the wrong on his behalf, the restitution brought before the LORD on his behalf shall belong to the priest, besides the ram of atonement with which atonement is made for him.
Every contribution from all the sacred gifts that the Israelites present to the priest shall belong to him.
Each man’s sacred gifts shall belong to him; whatever a man gives to the priest shall belong to the priest.”
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: If any man's wife goes astray and acts unfaithfully toward him,
“And a man has sexual intercourse with her, but it is hidden from her husband’s eyes and kept secret, though she has become defiled, and there is no witness against her, and she has not been caught;

and a spirit of jealousy comes over her husband and he becomes jealous of his wife when she has become defiled, or a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he becomes jealous of his wife when she has not become defiled—

the man shall bring his offering to the priest: one-tenth of a seah of barley flour. He must not pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance that brings sin to mind.
The priest shall bring her forward, and she shall stand before the LORD.
The priest shall take holy water in an earthenware vessel. He shall take some of the dust at the base of the altar and put it into the water.

The priest shall have the woman stand before the LORD, uncover her head, and place in her hands the grain offering of remembrance, the grain offering of jealousy. In the priest’s hand shall be the bitter water of testing.

The priest shall put the woman under oath and say to her, ‘If no man has slept with you, and you have not gone astray and become defiled with anyone other than your husband, be free from the harm of this bitter water of testing.
But if you have gone astray with someone other than your husband and have become defiled, and a man other than your husband has slept with you—’

the priest shall put the woman under an oath of cursing, and the priest shall say to the woman, ‘May the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people. May the LORD make your thighs waste away and your belly swell.
May this water of testing enter your belly, make your abdomen swell, and make your thighs waste away.’ And the woman shall say, ‘Amen, amen.’
The priest shall write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the water of testing.
He shall make the woman drink the bitter water that tests her, and the testing water shall enter her to test her.
The priest shall take the grain offering of jealousy from the woman's hands, set the grain offering apart before the Lord, and bring it to the altar.
The priest shall take the memorial portion from the grain offering and offer it on the altar. Then he shall make the woman drink the water.

If she has defiled herself and been unfaithful to her husband, the testing water shall enter her and test her. Her belly shall swell, and her thighs shall waste away. That woman shall become a curse among her people.
But if that woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she shall be cleared and shall bear a son.
This is the law concerning jealousy, when a woman strays from her husband and defiles herself,
or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he becomes jealous of his wife. He shall have the woman stand before the Lord, and the priest shall carry out this entire law for her.
That man shall be free from guilt, but that woman shall bear her guilt.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When a man or woman makes a special vow, a Nazirite vow, dedicating themselves to the Lord,
they shall abstain from wine and strong drink. They shall not drink wine vinegar or vinegar made from strong drink, nor shall they drink any grape infusion or eat grapes or raisins.
Throughout the days of their Nazirite dedication, they shall eat nothing produced by the grapevine, from the seeds to the skins.
Throughout the days of his Nazirite vow, no razor shall pass over his head. Until the days of his dedication to the Lord are completed, he shall be holy and shall let the hair of his head grow.
Throughout the days of his dedication to the Lord, he shall not go near a dead person.
He shall not make himself unclean for his father, his mother, his brother, or his sister when they die, because the crown of his God is upon his head.
Throughout all the days of his Nazirite vow, he is holy to the Lord.
If someone suddenly dies beside him, the head of his Nazirite dedication shall become unclean. He shall shave his head on the day of his cleansing; on the seventh day he shall shave it.
On the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a whole burnt offering. He shall make atonement for him for the sin he committed through contact with the dead person, and he shall consecrate his head that same day.
He shall dedicate the days of his Nazirite dedication before the Lord and bring a year-old lamb as an offering. The previous days shall not count, because his Nazirite dedication became unclean.
This is the law for the Nazirite: On the day when the days of his Nazirite dedication are completed, he shall be brought to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

He shall present his offering to the Lord: one year-old male lamb without blemish as a burnt offering, one year-old ewe lamb without blemish as a sin offering, and one ram without blemish as a peace offering,
and a basket of unleavened bread: sifted flour, [?] mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, together with their grain offering and their drink offering.
The priest shall present it before the Lord and offer his sin offering and his whole burnt offering.
He shall offer one ram as a peace offering to the Lord, together with the basket of unleavened bread. The priest shall also offer its grain offering and its drink offering.

At the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the Nazirite shall shave the head of his Nazirite dedication. He shall take the hair from the head of his Nazirite dedication and put it in the fire beneath the peace offering.

The priest shall take the boiled shoulder from the ram, one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and place them in the Nazirite’s hands after he has shaved off the hair of his dedication.

The priest shall set them apart as an offering before the Lord. They are holy and belong to the priest, in addition to the breast and thigh set apart as offerings. After this, the Nazirite may drink wine.
This is the law for the Nazirite who vows an offering to the Lord for his dedication, besides whatever else he can afford. He shall fulfill the vow he has made according to the law of his dedication.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to Aaron and his sons and tell them: This is how you shall bless the Israelites. Say to them:
May the Lord bless you and protect you.
May the Lord make his face shine upon you and give you life.
May the Lord lift up his face toward you and give you peace.
They shall place my name upon the Israelites, and I will bless them.
On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed it and consecrated it and all its furnishings. He also anointed and consecrated the altar and all its utensils.
The leaders of the Israelites, the heads of their ancestral households, brought offerings. These were the leaders of the tribes who supervised those who were counted.
They brought their offerings before the Lord: six fully equipped wagons and twelve oxen, one wagon for every two leaders and one ox for each leader. They presented them before the tabernacle.
The Lord said to Moses.
Accept these from them so that they may be used for the work at the Tent of Meeting. Give them to the Levites, to each according to his work.
Moses took the oxen and the wagons and handed them over to the Levites.
He gave two wagons and four oxen to the descendants of Gershon, according to their work.
He gave four wagons and eight oxen to the descendants of Merari, according to their work, under the supervision of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
He gave nothing to the descendants of Kohath, because the service of the holy things was entrusted to them, and they carried them on their shoulders.
The leaders brought the offering for the dedication of the altar on the day it was anointed. The leaders presented their offerings before the Lord.
The Lord said to Moses: One leader each day shall present his offerings for the dedication of the altar.
The one who presented his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, leader of the tribe of Judah.

His offering was one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
Also one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
Also one young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb for a burnt offering.
Also one male goat as a sin offering.
For the peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five young goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On the second day, Nethanel son of Zuar, leader of the tribe of Issachar, brought his offering.

His offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
Also one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
One young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb for a burnt offering.
And one male goat as a sin offering.
And for the sacrifice of peace offerings: two bulls, five rams, five young goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.
On the third day, Eliab son of Helon, the leader of the tribe of Zebulun, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one gold spoon weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.

Each silver dish weighed one hundred thirty shekels, and each bowl seventy. All the silver of the vessels weighed two thousand four hundred shekels, according to the sanctuary weight.
The twelve gold spoons were filled with incense. Each spoon weighed ten shekels, according to the sanctuary weight. All the gold of the spoons weighed one hundred twenty shekels.
All the bulls for the burnt offering numbered twelve, with twelve rams and twelve year-old lambs, together with their grain offerings, and twelve male goats for the sin offering.
All the bulls for the peace offering numbered twenty-four, with sixty rams, sixty young goats, and sixty year-old lambs. This was the dedication offering for the altar after it was anointed.
When Moses entered the tent of meeting, he heard the voice speaking with him from the mercy seat above the ark of the testimony. From between the two cherubim, it spoke with him.
The LORD spoke with Moses and said to him:
“Speak with Aaron and tell him: When you light the lamps, the seven lamps are to shine toward the front of the lampstand.”
Aaron did so with the seven lamps, facing the front of the lampstand. He lit its lamps as the LORD had commanded Moses.
This was how the lampstand was made: it was cast in gold, cast from its base to its top. He made the lampstand according to the pattern that the LORD had shown Moses.
The LORD spoke with Moses and said to him:
Take the Levites from among the Israelites and purify them.
“Do this to them to purify them: sprinkle the water of purification from sin on them. They must pass a razor over their entire bodies, wash their clothes, and purify themselves.
They must take one young bull, with its offering of one dish filled with fine flour mixed with oil. Present another young bull as a sin offering.
Bring the Levites before the tent of meeting, and assemble the entire congregation of the Israelites.
Bring the Levites before the LORD, and the Israelites must lay their hands on the Levites.
Aaron must set the Levites apart as an offering before the LORD from the Israelites, so that they may perform the LORD’s service.
The Levites must lay their hands on the head of the bull. Offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to make atonement for the Levites.
Have the Levites stand before Aaron and his sons, and set them apart as an offering to the Lord.
Separate the Levites from among the Israelites, and the Levites shall be mine.
Afterward the Levites shall enter and serve in the tent of meeting. Purify them and set them apart as an offering before the Lord.
For they are given to me as a gift from among the Israelites. In place of everyone who first opens the womb, the firstborn of all the Israelites, I have brought them near to myself.
For all the firstborn among the Israelites belong to me, both humans and livestock. On the day when I killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated them to myself.
I have brought the Levites near in place of the firstborn of the Israelites.

I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites, to perform the service of the Israelites in the tent of meeting and to make atonement for the Israelites, so that no sudden death will occur among the Israelites when they approach the sanctuary.
Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of the Israelites did this to the Levites. Just as the Lord commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so the Israelites did to them.
The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes. Aaron set the Levites apart as an offering before the Lord, and Aaron made atonement for them and purified them.
Afterward the Levites entered to perform their service in the tent of meeting before Aaron and his sons. Just as the Lord commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so the Israelites did to them.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
This shall be the law for the Levites: From twenty-five years old and upward, a Levite shall come to join the ranks in the service of the tent of meeting.
At fifty years old, he shall retire from the ranks of those serving and shall no longer perform the work.
He shall assist his brothers in the tent of meeting by keeping watch, but he shall not do the work. This is how you shall deal with the Levites concerning their duties.
The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after the Israelites came out of Egypt, and said to him:
The Israelites shall celebrate the Passover at its appointed time.
On the fourteenth day of this month, at twilight, they shall celebrate it at its appointed time. They shall celebrate it according to all its commandments and all its regulations.
Moses told the Israelites to celebrate the Passover.
They celebrated the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, at twilight, in the wilderness of Sinai. Just as the Lord commanded Moses, so the Israelites did.
There were men who were unclean because of a human corpse and could not celebrate the Passover on that day. They came before Moses and Aaron that day.
Those men said to them, "We are unclean because of contact with a human corpse. Why are we being kept from presenting the Lord's offering at its appointed time among the Israelites?"
Moses said to them, "Stay where you are, and I will hear what the Lord commands concerning you."
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: Any man who is unclean because of a dead body, or is on a distant journey, or is among your future generations, shall celebrate the Passover to the Lord.
They shall celebrate it on the fourteenth day of the second month, at twilight. They shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
They shall leave none of it until morning, and they shall not break any of its bones. They shall celebrate it according to every commandment concerning the Passover.

But if a man is clean and is not on a journey, yet does not celebrate the Passover at its appointed time, that person shall perish from among his people. Because he did not present the Lord's offering at its appointed time, that man shall bear his sin.

When someone who turns to me lives among you and celebrates the Passover to the Lord, he shall do so according to the commandment for the Passover and its regulations. There shall be one law for you, for the person who turns to me, and for the inhabitants of the land.

On the day the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered the tent of meeting and the area in front of the entrance of the testimony. In the evening, something like the appearance of fire was over the tabernacle until morning.
This was always the case: the cloud covered it by day, and the appearance of fire by night.
Whenever the cloud rose from the tabernacle, the Israelites would then set out. Wherever the cloud settled, there the Israelites would camp.
At the Lord’s command the Israelites would set out, and at the Lord’s command they would camp. As long as the cloud rested over the tabernacle, they remained in camp.
When the cloud remained over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites kept the Lord’s charge and did not set out.
Sometimes the cloud remained over the tabernacle for only a few days. At the Lord’s command they would camp, and at the Lord’s command they would set out.

Sometimes the cloud would remain over the tabernacle from evening until morning. When the cloud rose in the morning, they would set out. Whether by day or by night, when the cloud rose, they would set out.

Whether for days or months or from one season to another, as long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle, the Israelites would remain camped and would not set out. When the cloud rose, they would set out.
At the Lord’s command they would camp, and at the Lord’s command they would set out. They kept the Lord’s charge according to the Lord’s command through Moses.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
Make yourself two silver trumpets. Make them of cast metal. They shall be for you to summon the assembly and to signal the camps to set out.
They shall blow them, and the whole congregation shall assemble before you at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
If they sound just one, the leaders and the heads of Israel’s thousands shall gather before you.
They shall sound an alarm on the trumpet, and the camps stationed on the east shall set out.
They shall sound the horn a second time, and the camps stationed on the south shall set out. They shall blow the horn when they set out.
When you gather the assembly, sound the call, but do not sound the alarm.
The sons of Aaron the priest shall blow the trumpets. These shall be a lasting ordinance for you throughout your generations.
If war comes to your land against the oppressors who oppress you, sound an alarm on the trumpets. You will be remembered before the Lord your God and saved from your enemies.

On your days of rejoicing, at your festivals, and at the beginnings of your months, blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your peace offerings. They shall serve as a reminder for you before your God. I am the Lord your God.
In the second year, on the tenth day of the second month, the cloud rose from the tabernacle of the testimony.
The Israelites set out on their journeys from the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
They set out for the first time at the Lord’s command through Moses.
The division of the camp of Judah set out first, according to their military units. The commander of the army was Nahshon son of Amminadab.
The commander of the army of the tribe of Issachar was Nethanel son of Zuar.
The commander of the army of the tribe of Zebulun was Eliab son of Helon.
They took down the tabernacle, and the descendants of Gershon and the descendants of Merari set out, carrying the tabernacle.
The division of the camp of Reuben and their military units set out. The commander of the army was Elizur son of Shedeur.
The commander of the army of the tribe of Simeon was Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
The commander of the army of the tribe of Gad was Eliasaph son of Reuel.
The descendants of Kohath would set out, carrying the tabernacle. The tabernacle would be set up before they arrived.
The division of the camp of Ephraim set out according to their military units. The commander of the army was Elishama son of Ammihud.
The commander of the force of the tribe of Manasseh was Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
The commander of the forces of the tribe of Benjamin was Abidan son of Gideoni.
The standard of the camp of the Danites set out, gathering all the camps and their forces. The commander of the force of the tribe of the Danites was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
The commander of the forces of the tribe of Asher was Pagiel son of Ocran.
The commander of the force of the tribe of Naphtali was Ahira son of Enan.
These were the departures of the Israelites, according to their divisions.

Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are setting out for the place of which the Lord said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will treat you well, because the Lord has promised good things for Israel.”
He said to him, “I will not go. Instead, I will go to my own land, to the place where I was born.”
Moses said to him, “Do not leave us, because you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you will be our eyes.
If you go with us, we will share with you the good things the Lord does for us.”
They set out from the mountain of the Lord on a three-day journey. The ark of the Lord’s covenant traveled a day’s journey ahead of them to prepare a campsite for them.
The cloud of the Lord was above them by day whenever they set out from the camp.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say, “Rise up, Lord! Let those who hate you be shattered, and let your enemies flee before you.”
When it came to rest, he would say, “Return, Lord, to the tens of thousands and the thousands of Israel.”
When the people complained, it displeased the Lord. The Lord heard, and his anger flared up. The Lord’s fire blazed among them and consumed the outskirts of the camp.
The people cried out to Moses, and Moses prayed before the Lord, and the fire died down.
He named that place Taberah because the Lord’s fire had blazed among them.
The mixed crowd among them was overcome with craving, and they in turn made the Israelites weep too, saying, “Who will give us meat to eat?
We remember the fish we used to eat for free in Egypt, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic.
But now our strength is fading, and there is nothing before our eyes except this manna.”
The manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance was like that of bdellium.
The people went around gathering it. They ground it in a mill or pounded it in a mortar, cooked it in a pot, and made cakes from it. It tasted like something kneaded with oil.
When the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna fell on it.
Moses heard the people weeping in their families, each at the entrance to his tent. The Lord’s anger flared up, and Moses was displeased too.
Moses said to the Lord, “My Lord, why have you treated your servant badly? Why have I not found favor in your eyes, that you have placed the whole burden of this people on me?
Did I conceive all these people? Did I give birth to them, that you should say to me, ‘Carry them in your arms, as a caregiver carries an infant, to the land you swore to give their ancestors’?
Where can I get meat to give all these people? They weep before me and say, ‘Give us meat to eat.’
I cannot carry all these people by myself, because they are too much for me.
If this is how you treat me, kill me outright, if I have found favor in your eyes, and do not let me see my misery.

The Lord said to Moses, “Gather for me seventy men from the elders of Israel, whom you know to be the leaders and officers of the people. Bring them to the tent of meeting, and let them stand ready there with you.”

I will come down and speak with you there. I will take some of the spirit that is upon you and put it upon them. They will share with you the burden of these people, so that you will not carry it alone.

Moses said to the people, “Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, so that you may eat meat. For you wept before the Lord and said, ‘Who will give us meat to eat? We were better off in Egypt.’ The Lord will give you meat to eat.
You will eat it not for one day, or two days, or five days, or ten days, or twenty days.

You will eat it for a whole month, until it comes out of your nostrils and becomes loathsome to you, because you rejected the Lord who is among you, and wept before the Lord and said, ‘Why did we ever leave Egypt?’”
Moses said before the Lord, “The people among whom I am number six hundred thousand men on foot, yet you have said, ‘I will give them meat, and they will eat for a whole month.’
If sheep and cattle are slaughtered for them, what will that do for them? And if all the fish of the sea are caught for them, how will they be enough for them?”
The Lord said to Moses, “The Lord’s hand is sufficient. Now you will see whether my word comes true or not.”
Moses went out and told the people the Lord’s words. He gathered seventy men from the elders of the people and stationed them around the tabernacle.

The Lord came down in the cloud and spoke with him. He took some of the spirit that was upon him and put it upon the seventy elders. When the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, but they did not do so again.

Two men had remained in the camp. The name of one was Eldad, and the name of the other was Medad. The spirit rested upon them. They too were among those registered, but they had not come to the tabernacle. They prophesied in the camp.
A young man ran and reported to Moses, saying to him, “Look, Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!”
Hoshea son of Nun, Moses’ assistant from his youth, responded and said to him, “My lord Moses, stop them!”
Moses said to him, “Do not be jealous on my behalf. If only all the Lord’s people were prophets, with the Lord putting his spirit upon them!”
Moses returned to the camp, he and the elders of Israel.

A wind went out from the Lord and brought quail up from the sea and cast them over the camp, a day's journey in one direction and a day's journey in the other, all around the camp, about two cubits above the ground.
The people stayed up all that day, all night, and all the next day, gathering the quail. Whoever gathered the least gathered ten homers. They spread them out for themselves all around the camp.
While the meat was still between their teeth, before it had been swallowed, the Lord’s anger grew fierce against the people, and the Lord struck the people with a very great plague.
He named that place Graves of Craving, because there they buried the people who had given in to craving.
From Graves of Craving the people traveled to Hazeroth, and they stayed at Hazeroth.
Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married, for he had married a Cushite woman.
They said, “Has the Lord spoken only with Moses? Look, he has spoken with us too.” And the Lord heard.
Now the man Moses was very humble, more than anyone else on earth.
Suddenly the Lord said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “Come out, all three of you, to the tent of meeting.” And the three of them came out.
The Lord came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting. He called Aaron and Miriam, and the two of them came forward.
The Lord said to them, “Listen now to my words. If you have the gift of prophecy, I, the Lord, reveal myself to you in a vision and speak with you in a dream.
Not so with my servant Moses. He is faithful in all my house.
I speak with him mouth to mouth, in a vision and not through images, and he sees the glory of the Lord. Why were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?
The Lord's anger burned against them, and he departed.
The cloud withdrew from the tabernacle, and there was Miriam, leprous like snow. Aaron turned toward Miriam and saw that she was leprous.
Aaron said to Moses, “I beg you, my lord, do not hold this sin against us, for we have acted foolishly and sinned.
Do not let her be like a dead child coming out of its mother's womb with half its flesh eaten away.”
Moses cried out to the Lord and said, “Please, God, heal her!”
The Lord said to Moses, “If her father had spat in her face, would she not have been ashamed for seven days? Let her remain outside the camp for seven days, and then let her come in.”
Miriam remained outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not set out until Miriam had come back in.
Then the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
“Send men to spy out the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. Send one man from each ancestral tribe, each one a leader among them.”
Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran at the Lord's command. All of them were leaders of Israel.
These were their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
From the tribe of Simeon: Shaphat son of Haddi.
from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Issachar, Nagael son of Joseph;
from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Daphu;
from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddi son of Suri;
from the tribe of Joseph, from the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi;
from the tribe of Dan, Gamaliel son of Gemalli;
from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Malkiel;
from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machir.
These were the names of the men Moses sent to spy out the land. Moses called Hoshea son of Nun Joshua.
Moses sent them to spy out the land of Canaan and said to them, “Go up this way into the south, and go up into the hill country.
See what the land is like, and whether the people who live in it are strong or weak, few or many.
And what is the land like where they live?
Is it fertile, or are there trees in it or not? Be courageous and bring back some of the land’s fruit.” It was the season of the first ripe grapes.
They went up and spied out the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, at the entrance to Hamath.
They went up into the south and came to Hebron. Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, descendants of giants, were there. Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
They came to the Valley of the Cluster and cut from there a branch with a single cluster of grapes. Two of them carried it between them on a pole. They also took some pomegranates and figs.
They called that place the Valley of the Cluster because of the cluster that the Israelites cut there.
They returned from spying out the land after forty days.

They came to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of the Israelites in the wilderness of Paran, at Rekem. They brought back a report to him and to the whole congregation and showed them the fruit of the land.
They told him, “We went to the land where you sent us. It flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
But the people who live in the land are strong, and the towns are fortified and very large. We also saw descendants of giants there.
The Amalekites live in the southern region. The Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country. The Canaanites live beside the sea and along the Jordan.”
Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, “We must go up and take possession of it, because we can certainly overcome it.”
But the men who had gone up with him said, “We cannot go up against those people, because they are stronger than we are.”

Those who had spied out the land spread a report about it among the Israelites. They told them, “The land we passed through and spied out is a land that devours its inhabitants. All the people we saw in it are men of great size.
There we saw giants, sons of giants, who came from giants. We were like grasshoppers in their eyes; that is how we were in their eyes.”
The whole congregation cried out and raised their voices in weeping. The people wept that night.
All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron. The whole congregation said to them, “If only we had died in Egypt! Or in this wilderness—if only we had died!
Why is the Lord bringing us into this land to fall by the sword, while our wives and our dependents become plunder? We were better off when we were living in Egypt.”
They said to one another, “Come, let us appoint a leader for ourselves and return to Egypt.”
Moses and Aaron fell facedown before the entire assembly of the congregation of the Israelites.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had spied out the land, tore their clothes.
They said to the whole congregation of the Israelites, “The land we passed through to spy out is a very good land.
If the Lord is pleased with us, he will bring us into this land and give it to us—a land flowing with milk and honey.
Only do not rebel against the Lord, and do not be afraid of the people of the land, because they are bread for us. Their strength has left them, and the Lord is with us. Do not be afraid of them.”
The whole congregation said to stone them with stones. Then the glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud at the tent of meeting, in the sight of all the Israelites.
The Lord said to Moses, “How long will these people provoke me? How long will they refuse to believe me, despite all the signs I have performed among them?
I will strike them with a plague and destroy them, and I will make you into a nation greater and stronger than they are.”
Moses said to the Lord, “The Egyptians will hear that you brought these people up from among them by your power.

And the inhabitants of this land, who have heard, will say that you, Lord, are among these people; that you, Lord, have appeared eye to eye; that your cloud stands over them; and that you went ahead of them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
When you kill these people as though they were one man, the nations that have heard of your fame will say,
‘Because the Lord could not bring the people into the land he swore to give them, he slaughtered them in the wilderness.’
Now, Lord, let your power be shown to be great, just as you spoke, saying,

‘Lord, you are slow to anger and abundant in kindness. You forgive wrongdoing and sin, but you certainly do not acquit the guilty. You bring punishment for the fathers’ sins upon their children and their children’s children, to the third and fourth generations.’
Now forgive the wrongdoing of these people according to your abundant kindness, just as you have forgiven them from Egypt until now.”
The Lord said to Moses, “I have forgiven them as you asked.
But as surely as I live, and the glory of the Lord has filled the whole earth,
all the men who have seen my glory and the signs I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness, yet have tested me these ten times and have not obeyed my voice—
they will certainly not see the land I swore to give their fathers. None of those who provoke me will see it.
But my servant Caleb, because my spirit was with him and he followed me fully, I will bring into the land he entered, and his descendants will inherit it.
The Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the hill country. Tomorrow, turn back and set out for the wilderness along the road to the Red Sea.”
The Lord spoke with Moses and Aaron and said to them,
“How long will this wicked congregation grumble before me? I have heard the grumbling that the Israelites grumble before me.
Tell them, ‘As surely as I live, declares the Lord, I will do to you just as you have said in my presence.
Your corpses will fall in this wilderness—all of you who were numbered, all of you who were counted, from twenty years old and upward—because you grumbled against me.
You will not enter the land in which I raised my hand and swore to settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

Your dependents, whom you said would become plunder, and your children, who today do not know good from evil—they will enter the land. I will bring them in, and they will come to know the land you rejected.
But your own corpses will fall in this wilderness.
Your children will be shepherds in this wilderness for forty years and will bear the consequences of your unfaithfulness until your corpses have perished in this wilderness.
According to the number of days you explored the land—forty days, a year for each day—you will bear your wrongdoing for forty years. Then you will know that it is because you grumbled before me.
I, the Lord, have spoken. This is what I will do to this entire wicked congregation, you who have gathered before me: they will perish in this wilderness, and there they will die.
The men whom Moses sent to spy out the land returned and made the entire congregation grumble against him by spreading a bad report about the land.
The men who spread the bad report about the land died suddenly of a plague before the Lord.
But Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh survived out of those men who went to spy out the land.
Moses told all the Israelites these things, and the people sat in deep mourning.
They rose early in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain, saying, “Here we are, going up to the place the Lord told us about, for we have sinned.”
Moses said to them, “Why have you disobeyed the command spoken by the Lord? Because of this, you will not succeed.
Do not go up, because the Lord is not with you, so that you will not be defeated before your enemies.
For the Canaanites and Amalekites are there ahead of you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned away from following the Lord, the Lord will not be with you.”
They began to go up to the top of the mountain, but neither the ark of the Lord’s covenant nor Moses left the camp.
The Amalekites and Canaanites who lived on that mountain came down, struck them down, and pursued them as far as Hormah.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land where you will live, which I am giving you as an inheritance,
present an offering to the Lord, a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, or at your festivals. Make a pleasing aroma for the Lord from cattle or from the flock.
The one presenting his offering to the Lord shall present a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil.
Present a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering with the burnt offering or sacrifice of each lamb.
For each ram, prepare a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah mixed with a third of a hin of oil.
Present a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering, a sweet aroma to the Lord.
If you present a young bull as a whole burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a peace offering to the Lord,
present with the young bull a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah mixed with half a hin of oil.
Present half a hin of wine as a drink offering, an offering of a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Do this for each bull and each ram, or for a lamb from the sheep or from the goats.
According to the number you prepare, do the same for each one, according to their number.
Everyone of the house of Israel shall do these things in this way and present an offering of a sweet aroma to the Lord.
If someone who turns to me lives with you, or is among you throughout your generations, and makes an offering of a sweet aroma to the Lord, he shall do just as you do.
There shall be one law for you and for the one who turns to me and lives with you, a perpetual law throughout your generations. The one who turns to me shall be like you before the Lord.
You shall have one law and one rule, both for you and for those who turn to me and live among you.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land into which I am bringing you,
when you eat the bread of the land, set aside an offering for the Lord.
From the first of your dough, set aside [?] as an offering for the Lord. Set it aside just as you set aside an offering from the threshing floor.
Give the first of your dough as an offering to the Lord throughout your generations.
If you go astray and fail to carry out all these commandments that the Lord spoke to Moses,
everything that the Lord commanded you through Moses, from the day the Lord gave his commands onward throughout your generations,

if an error was committed without the assembly's knowledge, the whole assembly shall offer one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord, with its fine flour and its drink offering, as prescribed, and one male goat as a sin offering.

The priest shall make atonement for the whole assembly of the Israelites, and they shall be forgiven, because it was an error, and they have brought their offerings as an offering to the Lord, and an offering to the Lord for their sins, for their offenses.
The whole assembly of the Israelites shall be forgiven, along with those who turn to me and live in Israel, because the error belonged to the whole people.
If one person sins unintentionally, that person shall offer a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
The priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the person who sinned unintentionally. Atonement shall be made for that person, and that person shall be forgiven.
For the Israelites and for those who turn to me and live among you, you shall have one law for anyone who acts unintentionally.
But anyone who acts defiantly, whether one of you or one of those who turn to me, has blasphemed against the Lord. That person shall be destroyed from among their people.
Because that person has despised the Lord's words and disregarded his commandments, that person shall be destroyed, and their guilt shall rest on them.
While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
Those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole assembly.
They put him in custody, because it had not yet been made clear what should be done to him.
The Lord said to Moses, “The man must be put to death. The whole congregation shall stone him with stones outside the camp.”
The whole assembly took him outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them to make tassels for themselves on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and to put a blue cord in the tassels at their corners.

You shall have these tassels so that you may see them and remember all the commandments of the Lord your God and carry them out, and not go astray after your hearts and your thoughts, after which you stray.
You shall remember and carry out all my commandments and be holy to your God.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord your God.
Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, rebelled, along with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, descendants of Reuben.
They rose up before Moses, along with two hundred and fifty men from the Israelites, leaders of the congregation who were summoned to the assembly, men of renown.

They gathered against Moses and Aaron and said to them, “Is it not enough for you that the entire congregation is holy, every one of them, and the Lord is among them? Must you also exalt yourselves above the Lord’s entire congregation?”
When Moses heard this, he fell facedown.

He spoke to Korah and all his company and said to them, “In the morning the Lord will show who belongs to him. Whoever is holy will approach him, and whoever he chooses he will bring near to himself.”
“Do this: take incense burners for yourselves, you, Korah, and all your company.”
“Put fire in them and put incense in them before the Lord tomorrow. The man whom the Lord chooses will be holy. Enough from you, sons of Levi!”
Moses said to Korah, “Listen further, sons of Levi.”

“Is it not enough for you that the God of Israel has set you apart from the entire congregation of Israel and brought you near to himself to do the work of the Lord’s tabernacle and to stand before the congregation to serve them?”
“He has brought you near, along with all your fellow Levites. Yet you seek the priesthood too!”
Therefore, you and your whole congregation shall assemble before the Lord tomorrow. And Aaron—who is he that you complain against him?
Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said, “We will not come up.”
“Is it not enough for you that you brought us up from a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness? Must you also lord it over us?”
“You have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor have you given us fields and vineyards as an inheritance. Even if you put out our eyes, we will not come up.”
Moses was very angry and said to the Lord, “Do not look favorably on their offerings. I have not taken a donkey from a single one of them, nor have I harmed any of them.”
Moses said to Korah, “You and all your company must appear before the Lord tomorrow—you, they, and Aaron.”

“Each of you must take his incense burner, put fire in it, and put incense in it. Bring them before the Lord, each man with his incense burner, 250 incense burners. You and Aaron must also each bring his incense burner.”
Each man took his censer, and they put fire in them and placed incense in them. They stood before the tent of meeting with Moses and Aaron.
Korah assembled the entire congregation against them at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of the Lord appeared to the entire congregation.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
“Separate yourselves from this congregation, so that I may destroy them in an instant.”
They fell facedown and said, “O God, God of the spirits of all flesh, will one man sin and anger fall on the entire congregation?”
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Speak to the entire congregation and tell them, ‘Move away from the area around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.’”
Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.

He spoke to the entire congregation and said to them, “Get away from the tents of these sinful men. Do not go near anything that belongs to them, so that you will not be swallowed up because of their sins.”
They moved away from the dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrances to their tents, along with their wives, their sons, and their households.
Moses said, “By this you will know that the Lord sent me to do all these deeds, and that they did not come from my own mind.”
If these men die as everyone else dies, and the same fate befalls them as befalls everyone else, then the Lord has not sent me.

But if the Lord creates something new, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them and everything they have, and they and everything they have go down alive to Sheol, then you will know that these men have provoked the Lord to anger.
When Moses finished saying all these words, the ground beneath them split open.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, all the people who were with Korah, and all their possessions.
They and everything they had went down alive to Sheol. The earth closed over them, and they perished from among the assembly.
All the Israelites around them fled at the sound of their cries, saying, “The earth might swallow us too!”
Fire came out from before the Lord and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who were offering incense.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest: Take the censers from among those who were burned, and scatter the fire far away, because the censers have become holy.

Take the censers of these men who sinned at the cost of their own lives, and make them into thin sheets to cover the altar. Because they presented them before the Lord, they have become holy. They will be a sign among the Israelites.”
Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that the men who were burned had presented, and hammered them into sheets for the altar.

They were a reminder to the Israelites that no unauthorized man, anyone who was not a descendant of Aaron, should approach to offer fragrant incense before the Lord, so that he would not become like Korah and his entire assembly, just as the Lord had said through Moses.
The next day, the whole congregation of the Israelites complained against Moses and Aaron and said to them, “You have killed the Lord's people.”
When the whole assembly gathered against Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the tent of meeting and saw that the cloud had covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared.
Moses and Aaron came before the tent of meeting.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
“Separate yourselves from this assembly, so that I may destroy them in a single moment.” And they fell facedown.

Moses said to Aaron, “Take a censer, put fire in it, and put incense in it. Carry it quickly to the assembly and make atonement for them, because wrath has gone out from before the Lord, and a sudden plague has begun among the people.”
Aaron did as Moses told him and ran into the camp. He saw that a sudden plague had begun among the people, so he put on the incense and made atonement for the people.
He stood between the dead and the living, and the sudden plague was stopped.
Those who died in the sudden plague numbered fourteen thousand seven hundred, besides those who died in Korah’s rebellion.
Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance to the tent of meeting, and the sudden plague had been stopped.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Speak to the Israelites and take from them one staff for each ancestral house, from all their leaders according to their ancestral houses—twelve staffs. Write each man’s name on his staff.
Write Aaron's name on the staff of Levi, for there shall be one staff for each ancestral household.
Place them in the tent of meeting before the testimony, where I meet with you.
The staff of the man I choose will sprout, and I will rid myself of the Israelites’ grumbling, which they direct against you.”
Moses spoke to the Israelites, and all their leaders gave him a staff, one staff for each leader of their ancestral households, twelve staffs in all. Aaron’s staff was among their staffs.
Moses placed the staffs before the Lord in the tabernacle of the testimony.
The next day Moses entered the tabernacle of the testimony and saw that Aaron’s staff, belonging to the house of Levi, had sprouted. It had put out leaves and borne clusters of almonds.
Moses brought all the staffs out from before the Lord to all the Israelites. They looked, and each man took his staff.
The Lord said to Moses, “Put Aaron’s staff back before the testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebellious children, so that their grumbling against me may come to an end and they may not die.”
Moses did as the Lord commanded him; that is what he did.
The Israelites said to Moses, “Look, we are perishing! We are lost! We are all finished!
Everyone who approaches the Lord’s tabernacle dies. Look, we too are close to perishing!”

The Lord said to Aaron, “You, your sons, and your father’s household with you must bear the guilt connected with the sanctuary. You and your sons with you must bear the guilt connected with your priesthood.
Bring your brothers, the tribe of Levi, your father’s tribe, near with you, so that they may join you and serve you, while you and your sons with you are before the tabernacle of the testimony.
They must attend to your duties and the duties of the whole tabernacle. But they must not approach the sacred utensils or the utensils of the altar, so that neither they nor you may die.
They must join you and attend to the duties of the tent of meeting and all the service of the tabernacle. No outsider may approach you.
Attend to the duties of the sanctuary and the duties of the altar, so that wrath may not again come upon the Israelites.
Look, I have brought your brothers the Levites near from among the Israelites. They are a gift given to the Lord to perform the service of the tent of meeting.

You and your sons with you must guard your priesthood and all the prescribed arrangements of the altar. Perform the service inside the doorway. It is a gift that I have given to your priesthood. Any outsider who approaches must be put to death.

The Lord said to Aaron, “Look, I have given you charge of my contributions. All the holy offerings of the Israelites I have given to you by virtue of your anointing, to you and your sons with you, as a lasting ordinance.”

This shall be the sacred portion of the holy offerings from the fire: all their offerings, all their fine flour, all their sin offerings, and all their sacrifices that they present to me. They are most holy, belonging to you and your sons.
You must eat it in a most holy place. Every male may eat it. It shall be holy to you.

This is the portion set apart from your gifts. I have given all the portions set apart by the Israelites to you and to your sons and daughters with you, as a lasting ordinance. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat it.
All the best of the oil, and all the best of the grain and wine, their firstfruits that they give to the Lord, I have given to you.
All the firstfruits of their land that they bring to the Lord shall be yours. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat them.
Everything devoted to God in Israel shall be yours.

Every firstborn that opens the womb, of all flesh that they present to the Lord, whether human or animal, shall be yours. But you must redeem the human firstborn, and you must redeem the firstborn of unclean animals.
You must redeem them from the age of one month and upward, at a redemption price of fifty shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel. A shekel is twenty gerahs.

But you must not redeem the firstborn of cattle, sheep, or goats, because they are holy. Sprinkle their blood on the altar and offer up their fat as an offering on the altar, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Their meat shall be yours. Like the breast set apart as an offering and like the right thigh, it shall be yours.

All the portions of the holy things that the Israelites set apart for the Lord I have given to you and to your sons and daughters with you, as a lasting ordinance. It is an everlasting covenant of salt before the Lord for you and your descendants with you.

The LORD said to Aaron, “You shall inherit no land of theirs, and you shall have no share among them. But your share and your inheritance among the Israelites are the LORD’s contributions and his sacred offerings.”
“To the descendants of Levi I have given all the tithes of the Israelites as an inheritance, in return for the service they perform in the tent of meeting.
The Israelites must no longer approach the tent of meeting, lest they incur guilt and die.

The Levites shall perform the service of the tent of meeting, and they shall bear their guilt. This is a lasting ordinance throughout their generations. They shall receive no inheritance among the Israelites.
For I have given the Levites as an inheritance the tithes that the Israelites set apart for the LORD. That is why I told them that they would receive no inheritance among the Israelites.”
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:

“Speak to the Levites and tell them: When you receive from the Israelites the tithes that I have given you from them as an inheritance, set apart from them a contribution to the LORD, a tenth of the tithes.
Your contribution will be credited to you like grain from the threshing floor and like a contribution from the winepress.
In this way you too shall set apart a contribution to the LORD from all the tithes you receive from the Israelites. From them you shall give the LORD’s contribution to Aaron the priest and his sons.
From all the gifts you receive, set apart the entire contribution due to the LORD, from all the best of them—the portion of them to be consecrated.
