Tell them: When you set apart the best of it, the rest will be credited to the Levites like the produce of the threshing floor and the produce of the winepress.
You and the members of your households may eat it anywhere, because it is your wages in return for your service in the tent of meeting.
You will incur no guilt on account of it when you set apart the best of it. You must not defile the sacred offerings of the Israelites, lest you die.”
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
“This is the requirement of the law that the LORD has commanded: Tell the Israelites to bring you a red cow, sound and without defect, that has never had a yoke placed on it.
Give it to Eleazar the priest. It shall be taken outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence.
Eleazar the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and sprinkle some of its blood toward the front of the tent of meeting seven times.
He shall burn the cow before him. He shall burn its hide, its blood, and its flesh, together with its dung.
The priest shall take cedarwood, hyssop, and scarlet dye and throw them into the fire in which the cow is burning.
The priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Then he may enter the camp, but the priest will remain unclean until evening.
The person who burns the cow shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he will remain unclean until evening.

A man who is clean shall gather the cow's ashes and place them outside the camp in a clean place. They shall be kept for the whole congregation of the Israelites, reserved for the water of sprinkling, because it is a sin offering.
The person who gathers the cow’s ashes shall wash his clothes and remain unclean until evening. This shall be a permanent law for the Israelites and for those who turn to me and live among you.
Anyone who touches the dead body of any human being will be unclean for seven days.
He shall be sprinkled on the third day and on the seventh day, and he will become clean. But if he is not sprinkled on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not become clean.

Anyone who touches the dead body of any person who has died and is not sprinkled defiles the LORD’s tabernacle. That person shall be cut off from Israel. Because the water for sprinkling was not sprinkled on him, he will remain unclean, and his uncleanness remains upon him.
This is the law when a person dies in a tent: everyone who enters the tent, and everyone who is in the tent, will be unclean for seven days.
Every open vessel that has not been sealed is unclean.
Anyone who, in the open field, touches someone killed by the sword, a dead body, a human bone, or a grave will be unclean for seven days.
For the unclean person they shall take some ashes from the burning of the sin offering and pour fresh running water over them in a vessel.”

A clean man shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on the utensils, on all the people who were there, and on anyone who touched a bone, someone killed, a dead person, or a grave.

The clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. He shall sprinkle him on the seventh day, and he shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be clean in the evening.

If a man is unclean and has not been sprinkled, that person shall be cut off from his community, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the Lord. The water for sprinkling has not been sprinkled on him; he is unclean.
This shall be a permanent law for you. Whoever sprinkles the water for sprinkling shall wash his clothes, and whoever touches the water for sprinkling will be unclean until evening.
Whatever the unclean person touches will be unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening.
The Israelites, the whole congregation, came to the wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people stayed at Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.
There was no water for the people to drink, and the people gathered against Moses and Aaron.
The people quarreled with Moses and said to him, “If only we had died in the plague that killed our brothers before the Lord!
Why have you brought the Lord’s congregation into this wilderness, so that we and our livestock should die here?
Why did you bring us up from Egypt and bring us to this terrible place? It is no place for sowing, nor for vines, fig trees, or pomegranates, and there is no water to drink.”
Moses and Aaron went away from the congregation to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and fell on their faces. The glory of the Lord appeared to them.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him,

“Take the staff and gather the congregation, you and your brother Aaron. Speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will give its water. Bring water out of the rock for them, and give the congregation and their livestock something to drink.”
Moses took the staff from before the Lord, as he had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron gathered the whole congregation beside the rock, and he said to them, “Listen now, you grumblers! Shall we bring water out of this rock for you?”
Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff. A great deal of water came out, and all the people and their livestock drank.
The Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you did not trust me and show me to be holy before the Israelites, you shall not bring this congregation into the land I have given them.”
These are the waters of quarreling, where the Israelites quarreled before the Lord, and he showed himself holy among them.
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: “This is what your brother Israel says: You know all the hardship that has overtaken us.
Our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt for a long time. The Egyptians mistreated us and our ancestors.
We prayed before the Lord, and he heard our voice. He sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are at Kadesh, a town at the edge of your territory.

Now let us pass through your land. We will not pass through fields or vineyards, and we will not drink water from wells. Instead, we will travel along the King’s Highway, and we will not turn aside to the right or to the left until we have passed through your territory.”
Edom said to him, “You shall not pass through my territory, or I will come out against you with the sword.”
The Israelites said to him, “We will go up along the road. If we or our livestock drink any of your water, we will pay for it. We will only pass through on foot.”
Edom said, “You shall not pass through.” Edom came out against them with a powerful army and a strong hand.
Edom refused to let the Israelites pass through its territory, so Israel turned away from it.
They set out from Rekem, and the Israelites, the whole community, came to Mount Hor.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom:

“Aaron will be gathered to his people, for he will not enter the land I have given the Israelites, because you rebelled against my command at the waters of strife and did not uphold my holiness before their eyes at the waters.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor.
Remove Aaron’s clothes and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered and die there.”
Moses did as the Lord commanded him. They went up Mount Hor in the sight of the whole community.
Moses removed Aaron’s clothes and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron died there on Mount Hor, and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
The whole community saw that Aaron had died, and the entire house of Israel mourned Aaron for thirty days.
The Canaanite king of Gadar, who lived in the south, heard that Israel was coming along the spies’ route. He fought against Israel and took some of them captive.
Israel made a vow to the Lord, saying, “If you will indeed hand this people over to me, I will devote their towns to destruction.”
The Lord listened to Israel and handed the Canaanites over to them. They devastated them and devoted both them and their towns to destruction. They named that place Hormah.
They set out from Mount Hor along the route to the Red Sea to go around the land of Edom. The people grew impatient along the way.
The people grumbled against God and against Moses, saying, “Why have you brought us up from Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread and no water, and we are sick of this meager bread.”
The Lord sent venomous snakes among the people, and they bit the people. Many Israelites died.
The people came to Moses and said to him, “We have sinned by grumbling against the Lord and also against you. Pray to the Lord to rid us of the snakes.” So Moses prayed for the people.
The Lord said to Moses, “Make yourself a venomous snake out of bronze and set it up as a sign. Everyone who is bitten by a snake will look at it and live.”
Moses made a bronze snake and set it up as a sign. Whenever a snake bit someone, that person would look at the bronze snake and live.
The Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at the Spring of the Hebrews, in the wilderness facing Moab, toward the east, toward the sunrise.
From there they set out and camped in the valley of Zered.

From there they set out and camped on the other side of the Arnon, in the wilderness extending from the territory of the Amorites. For the Arnon is the boundary of the Moabites, between the Moabites and the Amorites.
For this reason it is said in the Book of the Wars of the Lord: “A flame in the whirlwind and in the valley of the Arnon.
He established the valleys that sloped toward the settlement of Ad and adjoined the border of the Moabites.”
There was the well, the well about which the Lord said to Moses, “Gather the people for me, and I will give them water.”
Then Israel sang this song: “Rise up, O well! Sing to it!
The well that the princes dug, that the rulers of the people dug out and explored with their staffs.” From the wilderness it was given as a gift.
From Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth.
From Bamoth in the valley in the countryside of Moab, to the top of the height overlooking Jeshimon.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites and said to him,

“Let me pass through your land. We will not turn aside into fields or vineyards, and we will not drink water from the wells. We will travel only along the King's Highway until we have passed through your territory.”
But Sihon would not allow Israel to pass through his territory. Sihon gathered his entire army and went out into the wilderness to meet Israel. He came to Jahaz and fought against Israel.
Israel struck him down with the sword and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites, because the border of the Ammonites was strongly defended.
Israel captured all these towns, and Israel settled in all the towns of the Amorites, in Heshbon and all its villages.
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites. He had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land, from his border to the Arnon.
That is why those who speak in proverbs say: “Come into Heshbon! Let the city of Sihon be built and established.
For fire went out from Heshbon, and a flame from the stronghold of Sihon. It consumed Ad [?] of Moab and those who worship at the high places of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Arnon! Woe to you, Moab! You have perished, people of Chemosh! He has given his sons as hostages and his daughters as captives to Sihon king of the Amorites.
The fields of Heshbon perished as far as Ribon [?] and lay desolate as far as Nekah [?] in the wilderness.”
Israel settled in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to spy out Jazer. He captured its villages and destroyed the Amorites who were there.
They turned and went up to the land of Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out to meet them, he and all his people, for battle at Edrei.
The LORD said to Moses, “Do not be afraid of him, for I am handing him, all his people, and all his land over to you. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
They destroyed him, his sons, and all his people, leaving him no survivor, and they took possession of his land.
The Israelites set out and camped in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor saw everything Israel had done to the Amorites.
The Moabites were very afraid of the people because they were so numerous. The Moabites were distressed because of the Israelites.

Moab said to the elders of Midian, “Now this multitude will graze on everything around us, as an ox grazes on the green plants of the field.” Balak son of Zippor was king of the Moabites at that time.

He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, who was by the river in the land of the Ammonites, to summon him and say to him, “Look, a people has come out of Egypt and covered the face of the land. They are now camped opposite me.

Now come and curse this people for me, because they are stronger than I am. Perhaps we can strike some of them down and drive them out of the land. For I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed.”
The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went with their divination fees in their hands. They came to Balaam and told him Balak’s words.
He said to them, “Spend the night here, and I will give you an answer according to what the Lord tells me.” So the officials of Moab stayed with Balaam.
God came to Balaam and said to him, “Who are these men with you?”
Balaam said to God, “Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent word to me, saying:
‘Look, a people has come out of Egypt and covered the face of the earth. Now come and curse them for me. Perhaps I will be able to fight against them and destroy them.’”
God said to Balaam, “Do not go with them, and do not curse the people, because they are blessed.”
Balaam got up in the morning and said to Balak’s officials, “Go back to your own land, because the Lord is not willing to let me go with you.”
The officials of Moab set out, came to Balak, and said to him, “Balaam refused to come with us.”
Balak again sent messengers, more important and distinguished than the earlier ones.
They came to Balaam and said to him, “This is what Balak son of Zippor says: ‘Do not let anything keep you from coming to me.’”
“For I will honor you greatly and do whatever you tell me. Come and curse this people for me.”
Balaam answered Balak’s servants, “Even if Balak gives me his house full of silver or gold, I cannot go against the command spoken by the Lord my God, in anything small or great.”
Now you too stay here tonight, and I will find out what more the Lord will say to me.
God came to Balaam at night and said to him, “If these men have come to summon you, get up and go with them. But do only what I tell you.”
Balaam got up in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the officials of Moab.
God’s anger burned against him because he went, and the angel of the Lord stood in the road to oppose him. He was riding his donkey, and his two young servants were with him.

The donkey saw the angel of the Lord standing in the road, holding his drawn sword in his hand. The donkey turned off the road and went into the field, and Balaam struck the donkey to turn her back onto the road.
The angel of the Lord stood in a vineyard path, with a wall on one side and a wall on the other.
The donkey saw the angel of the Lord and pressed against the wall, crushing Balaam’s foot against the wall. He struck her again.
The angel of the Lord went farther and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn aside, either to the right or to the left.
The donkey saw the angel of the Lord and lay down under Balaam. Balaam’s anger burned, and he struck the donkey with a stick.
The Lord opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you have struck me these three times?”
Balaam said to the donkey, “Because you have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hands, I would kill you now.”
The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey, which you have ridden from your youth until today? Have I ever done this to you before?” He said to her, “No.”
The Lord opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the Lord standing in the road, holding his drawn sword in his hand. He knelt and bowed down with his face to the ground.
The angel of the Lord said to him, “Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Look, I have come out to oppose you because you have set your course against me.
The donkey saw me and turned aside before me these three times. If she had not turned aside before me, I would have killed you by now, but I would have kept her alive.”
Balaam said to the angel of the Lord, “I have sinned. I did not know that you were standing in the road to oppose me. Now, if this is wrong in your eyes, I will turn back.”
The angel of the Lord said to Balaam, “Go with the men, but do only what I tell you.” So Balaam went with Balak’s officials.
Balak heard that Balaam had come and went out to meet him at the city of Moab, which was on the Arnon border, at the edge of the territory.
Balak said to Balaam, “Look, I sent word to summon you. Why did you not come to me? Perhaps you thought that I did not have the power to honor you.”
Balaam said to Balak, “Look, I have come to you. But now, can I really say anything? I will speak only the words God puts in my mouth.”
Balaam went with Balak, who brought him to Kiriath-huzoth.
Balak slaughtered cattle and sheep and sent some to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
In the morning, Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal. From there he saw the outskirts of the people.
Balaam said to Balak, “Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
Balak did as Balaam told him. Balaam and Balak offered bulls and rams on the altars.
Balaam said to Balak, “Stand here beside your burnt offerings while I go. Perhaps the Lord will come to meet me. Whatever message he shows me, I will tell you.” And he went alone.
God appeared to Balaam, and he said to him, “I have prepared seven altars and offered bulls and rams on the altars.”
The Lord put a word in Balaam’s mouth and said to him, “Go to Balak and speak this way.”
He came to him, and there he was, standing beside his burnt offerings, with all the officials of Moab.
He took up his oracle and said, “Balak, king of the Moabites, brought me from Aram, from the mountains of the east. He said to me, ‘Come, curse Jacob for me. Come, destroy Israel for me.’
How can I curse someone whom God has not cursed? How can I destroy someone whom the Lord has not destroyed?
For I have seen them from the mountain peaks and looked at them from the hills. Look, a people dwelling alone, not counted among the nations!
Who can count the dust of Jacob or number even a quarter of Israel? May I die the death of their upright people, and may my end be like theirs!”
Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I called you to curse my enemies, and here you are blessing them!”
Balaam answered, “Look, whatever the Lord puts in my mouth, that is what I am careful to speak.”
Balak said to him, “Come with me to another place, from which you can see them. You will see only their outskirts, not all of them. Curse them for me from there.”
He took him to the field of the lookout, to the top of the hill. He built seven altars and offered bulls and rams on the altars.
Balaam said to Balak, “Stand here beside your burnt offerings while I go over there.”
The Lord appeared to Balaam, put a word in his mouth, and said to him, “Go to Balak and say this to him.”
He came to him, and there he was, standing beside his burnt offerings, with the officials of Moab beside him. Balak said to him, “What did the Lord say?”
He took up his oracle and said, “Rise, Balak, and listen! Pay attention to my testimony, son of Zippor!
God is not a man who lies, nor a human being who changes his mind. He speaks and acts, and his word stands forever.
Look, I was brought here to bless, and I will not reverse the blessing.
I see no wrongdoing in Jacob, and I see no perversity in Israel. The Lord their God is with them, and the praise of their king is among them.
God, who brought them out of Egypt in his strength and majesty.
For there is no sorcery in Jacob, nor divination in Israel. At a time like this, Jacob and Israel will be told what God has done.
Look, the people rise like a lion and lift themselves up like a lion. They will not lie down until they have eaten prey and drunk the blood of the slain.
Balak said to Balaam, “Do not curse them at all, and do not bless them at all.”
Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not tell you that whatever the LORD tells me, that is what I do?”
Balak said to Balaam, “Come, I will take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God for you to curse them for me from there.”
Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks Jeshimon.
Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
Balak did as Balaam told him, and offered bulls and rams on the altars.
Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord to bless Israel. He did not go as he had before to seek omens, but turned his face toward the wilderness.
Balaam raised his eyes and saw Israel camped tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God came upon him.
He took up his poetic declaration and said, “Balaam son of Beor declares; the man whose eye is open declares.”
The one who hears the word of God declares, the one who sees a vision of God, fallen down with his eyes open.
How beautiful is your tent, Jacob, and your dwellings, Israel!
Like flowing streams, like a garden beside a river, like a tent that the LORD pitched, and like cedars beside the water.
A man will come forth from his sons, and his descendants will be amid abundant waters. The king will be exalted above Agag, and his kingdom will be exalted.
God brought them out of Egypt in his strength and majesty. He will devour the nations that hate him, break their bones, and cut through their loins.
He crouched and lay down like a lion, like a young lion—who will rouse him? Those who bless you are blessed, and those who curse you are cursed.
Balak’s anger burned against Balaam, and he clapped his hands. Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, but here you are blessing them—three times now!
“Now get out and go home! I said I would greatly honor you, but the LORD has kept you from receiving honor.”
Balaam answered Balak, “I also told the messengers you sent to me,
‘Even if Balak gives me his house full of silver or gold, I cannot go against the word of the LORD’s mouth and do good or evil of my own accord. Whatever the LORD tells me, that is what I say.’
“Now I am going back to my own land. But come, let me advise you about what this people will do to your people in the days to come.”
He took up his poetic declaration and said, “Balaam son of Beor declares; the man whose eye is open declares.”
The one who hears the word of God declares, the one who knows the knowledge of the Most High and sees a vision of God, fallen down with his eyes open.

I saw him, but not now; I beheld him, but he was not near. A star will rise from Jacob, and a leader will arise from Israel. He will destroy the mighty men of Moab and subdue all the descendants of Seth.
Edom will become his possession, and Seir, the possession of his enemies, will be his. Israel will gain strength.
He will come down from Jacob and destroy anyone who escapes from the city.
He saw Amalek and took up his oracle, saying, “Amalek was the first of the nations, but in the end it will perish forever.”
He saw the Kenites and took up his oracle, saying, “Your dwelling is secure, and your nest is set in the cliff.
“If Kain is given over to burning, they will take you captive as far as Assyria.”
He took up his oracle and said, “Alas! Who will live when God brings these things about?”
Legions will come out from the land of the Kittim. They will subjugate Assyria, and they will also subjugate the Hebrews. They too will perish forever.
Balaam got up, turned back, and went to his own land. Balak also went on his way.
Israel stayed at Shittim, and the people began to engage in sexual immorality with the daughters of Moab.
The women invited the people to the sacrifices offered to their gods. The people ate and bowed down to their gods.
Israel joined itself to Baal of Peor, and the LORD’s anger burned against the Israelites.
The LORD said to Moses, “Take all the leaders of the people and expose them before the LORD in full sunlight, so that my fierce anger may turn away from the Israelites.”
Moses said to the judges of Israel, “Each of you must kill his men who have joined themselves to Baal of Peor.”

Just then, a man from among the Israelites came forward before his fellow Israelites and went in to a Midianite woman, in the sight of Moses and the whole congregation of the Israelites. They were weeping at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw him. He rose from among the congregation and took a spear in his hand.
He followed the Israelite man into the chamber and pierced both of them—the Israelite man and the woman through her belly—in the chamber. Then the sudden plague was stopped among the Israelites.
Those who died in the sudden plague numbered twenty-four thousand.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the Israelites. He was zealous with my zeal among them, so I did not destroy the Israelites in my zeal.
Therefore I have said: Look, I am giving him a covenant of peace.
It will be for him and his descendants after him a covenant of everlasting priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.”
The name of the slain Israelite man who was killed with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, the head of an ancestral household of the tribe of Simeon.
The name of the Midianite woman was Cozbi daughter of Zur. He was the head of a people, of her ancestral household in Midian.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Harass the Midianites and destroy them,

because they harass you with the schemes they devised against you in the affair of Peor and in the affair of Cozbi, the daughter of a leader of Midian, their sister, who was killed on the day of the sudden plague in the affair of Peor.”
And it happened after the sudden plague.
The LORD said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest:
Take a census of the whole congregation of the Israelites, from twenty years old and upward, by their ancestral households—all in Israel who go out with the army.
Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan at Jericho.
Moses counted them from twenty years old and upward, as the LORD had commanded Moses and the Israelites who had come out of the land of Egypt.
Reuben was Israel’s firstborn. The descendants of Reuben: Hanoch, the clan of Hanoch; Pallu, the clan of Pallu;
Hezron, the clan of Hezron; Carmi, the clan of Carmi.
These were the clans of Reuben. Their number was forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty.
And the sons of Pallu: Eliab.
The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These were the prominent men of the congregation who rebelled against Moses and Aaron with Korah’s congregation, and rebelled against the Lord.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and Korah in the plague on the assembly, when the fire consumed two hundred and fifty men. And they became a warning sign.
But the sons of Korah did not die.
The sons of Simeon according to their clans: Jemuel, the clan of Jemuel; Jamin, the clan of Jamin; Jachin, the clan of Jachin.
Zerah, the clan of Zerah; Shaul, the clan of Shaul.
These are the clans of Simeon: twenty-two thousand two hundred.
The sons of Gad according to their clans: Zephon, the clan of Zephon; Haggi, the clan of Haggi; Shuni, the clan of Shuni.
Ozni, the clan of Ozni; Adi, the clan of Adi.
Arodi, the clan of Arodi; Adiel, the clan of Adiel.
These are the clans of the sons of Gad, according to their count: forty thousand five hundred.
The sons of Judah were Er and Onan. Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
The sons of Judah according to their clans were: Shelah, the clan of Shelah; Perez, the clan of Perez; Zerah, the clan of Zerah.
The sons of Perez were: Hezron, the clan of Hezron; Hamul, the clan of Hamul.
These are the clans of the sons of Judah, according to their count: seventy-six thousand five hundred.
The sons of Issachar according to their clans: Tola, the clan of Tola; Puah, the clan of Puah.
Jashub, the clan of Jashub; Shimron, the clan of Shimron.
These were the clans of Issachar according to their census: sixty-four thousand three hundred.
The sons of Zebulun according to their clans: Sered, the clan of Sered; Elon, the clan of Elon; Nahliel, the clan of Nahliel.
These are the clans of Zebulun, according to their count: sixty thousand five hundred.
The sons of Joseph according to their clans: Manasseh and Ephraim.
The sons of Manasseh: Machir, the clan of Machir. Machir fathered Gilead. Gilead, the clan of Gilead.
These were the sons of Gilead: Iezer, the clan of Iezer; Helek, the clan of Helek.
Ashdiel, the clan of Ashdiel; Shechem, the clan of Shechem.
Shemida, the clan of Shemida; Hepher, the clan of Hepher.
Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters. The names of Zelophehad’s daughters were Mahlah, [?], Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These are the clans of Manasseh and their count: fifty-two thousand seven hundred.
The sons of Ephraim according to their clans: Shuthelah, the clan of Shuthelah; Becher, the clan of Becher; Tahan, the clan of Tahan.
And these were the descendants of Shuthelah: Edan, the clan of Edan.
These were the clans of the descendants of Ephraim, numbering 32,500. These were the descendants of Joseph according to their clans.
The descendants of Benjamin according to their clans: Bela, the clan of Bela; Ashbel, the clan of Ashbel; Ahiram, the clan of Ahiram.
Shupham, the clan of Shupham; Huppim, the clan of Huppim.
The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: Ard, the clan of Ard; Naaman, the clan of Naaman.
These were the descendants of Benjamin, numbering 45,600.
The descendants of Dan according to their clans: Shuham, the clan of Shuham. These were the clans of Dan according to their clans.
The entire clan of Shuham numbered 64,400.
The descendants of Asher according to their clans: Imnah, the clan of Imnah; Ishvah, the clan of Ishvah; Ishvi, the clan of Ishvi; Beriah, the clan of Beriah.
The descendants of Beriah: Heber, the clan of Heber; Malchiel, the clan of Malchiel.
The name of Asher’s daughter was Serah.
These were the clans of the descendants of Asher, numbering 53,400.
The descendants of Naphtali according to their clans: Nahziel, the clan of Nahziel; Guni, the clan of Guni.
Jezer, the clan of Jezer; Shillem, the clan of Shillem.
These were the clans of the descendants of Naphtali according to their clans. Their number was 45,400.
The total number of Israelites counted was 601,730.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
The land shall be divided among these as an inheritance according to the number of names.
For the larger groups, increase their inheritance; for the smaller groups, reduce their inheritance. Each shall receive an inheritance according to the number counted.
But the land must be divided by lot. They shall inherit it according to the names of their ancestral tribes.
The inheritance shall be divided by the decision of the lot between the larger and smaller groups.
These were the Levites counted according to their clans: Gershon, the clan of Gershon; Kohath, the clan of Kohath; Merari, the clan of Merari.
These were the clans of the Levites: the clan of the Libnites, the clan of the Hebronites, the clan of the Mahlites, the clan of the Mushites, and the clan of Korah. Kohath fathered Amram.
The name of Amram’s wife was Jochebed, a daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt. She bore Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam to Amram.
Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar were born to Aaron.
Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord.
Their total was twenty-three thousand, counting every male from one month old and upward. They were not counted among the Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites.
These were those counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who counted the Israelites on the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
Among these there was not a single man from those counted by Moses and Aaron the priest when they counted the Israelites in the wilderness of Sinai.
For the Lord had told them, “They will surely be killed in the wilderness, and not one man among them will remain except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.”

The daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the clan of Manasseh son of Joseph, came forward. These were the names of his daughters: Mahlah, [?], Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They stood before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, before the leaders, and before the whole assembly at the entrance to the tent of meeting, and said,
“Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the assembly that rose up against the Lord in Korah’s assembly, but died for his own sins. He had no sons.
Why should our father’s name disappear from his clan because he has no son? Give us an inheritance among our father’s brothers.”
Moses brought their case before the Lord.
The Lord said to Moses.
The daughters of Zelophehad speak rightly. Give them a possession and an inheritance among their father’s brothers, and establish their father’s inheritance for them.
“And tell the Israelites: When a man dies and has no son, give his inheritance to his daughter.
If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers.
If he has no brothers, give his inheritance to his paternal uncles.
If he has no paternal uncle, give his inheritance to his nearest relative in his clan, and he shall inherit it. This shall be a legal statute for the Israelites, as the Lord commanded Moses.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Go up this mountain of Abarim and see the land of Canaan, which I have given to the Israelites.
See it, and then you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was gathered.

For you rebelled against my command in the wilderness of Zin, during the assembly’s dispute, and did not show me to be holy before their eyes at the waters.” These are the waters of dispute at Rekem in the wilderness of Zin.
Moses spoke before the Lord and said,
May the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation.
“Who will go out before them and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the Lord’s assembly will not be like sheep without a shepherd.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man who has the spirit in him, and lay your hand on him.
Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole assembly, and commission him before their eyes.
Give him some of your honor, so that the whole assembly of the Israelites will obey him.

He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall seek a ruling for him by inquiry before the Lord. At his command they shall go out, and at his command they shall come in—he and all the Israelites with him, the whole assembly.”
Moses did as the Lord commanded him. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole assembly.
He laid his hand on him and commissioned him, as the Lord commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him,
“Command the Israelites and tell them: They must take care to present my offerings, the food of my offerings, and the pleasing aroma to me at their appointed times.
Tell them: This is the offering you shall present to the Lord: two year-old lambs without blemish each day, regularly, as a whole burnt offering.
Offer one lamb in the morning, and offer the other lamb at twilight.
And one-tenth of a seah of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with a quarter of a hin of pressed oil.
This is the regular whole burnt offering established at Mount Sinai, an offering to the Lord with a pleasing aroma.
Its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin of wine for each lamb. In the sanctuary, a drink offering of aged wine shall be poured out before the Lord.
Offer the other lamb at twilight. Offer it with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
On the Sabbath day, offer two year-old lambs without blemish, and two-tenths of a seah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, together with its drink offering.
This is the whole burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the regular whole burnt offering and its drink offering.
At the beginning of your months, present whole burnt offerings to the Lord: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old lambs without blemish.
For each bull, offer three-tenths of a seah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and for each ram, two-tenths of a seah of fine flour mixed with oil.
For each lamb, offer one-tenth of a seah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering. This is a whole burnt offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

Their drink offerings shall be wine: half a hin for each bull, a third of a hin for each ram, and a quarter of a hin for each lamb. This is the whole burnt offering at the beginning of each month throughout the months of the year.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering to the Lord. It shall be offered in addition to the regular whole burnt offering and its drink offering.
On the fourteenth day of the first month is the Lord's Passover.
On the fifteenth day of that month is a festival. Unleavened bread shall be eaten for seven days.
The first day is a sacred assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.
Present an offering of whole burnt offerings to the Lord: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old lambs. They must be without blemish.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil. Prepare three-tenths of a seah for each bull and two-tenths of a seah for the ram.
Offer one-tenth of a seah for each lamb. Do this for all seven lambs.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you.
You shall offer these in addition to the morning whole burnt offering, the regular whole burnt offering.

You shall do these things every day for seven days, as an offering of food with a pleasing aroma to the Lord. It shall be offered in addition to the regular whole burnt offering and its drink offering.
On the seventh day you shall have a sacred assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.
On the day of the firstfruits, when you present fine flour from the new harvest to the Lord at your Festival of Weeks, you shall have a sacred assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.
Present whole burnt offerings with a pleasing aroma to the Lord: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old lambs.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of a seah for each bull and two-tenths of a seah for the ram.
And one-tenth of a seah for each lamb; do the same for all seven lambs.
And one male goat to make atonement for you.
Besides the regular whole burnt offering and its grain offering, you shall offer animals without defect, along with their drink offerings.
On the first day of the seventh month, you shall have a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work. It shall be a day of trumpet blasts for you.
Offer whole burnt offerings as a pleasing aroma to the Lord: one young bull, one ram, and seven year-old lambs, without defect.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of a measure for the bull and two tenths of a measure for the ram.
And one tenth of a measure for each lamb, for all seven lambs.
And one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.

These are in addition to the whole burnt offering for the new moon and its grain offering, and the regular whole burnt offering, with their grain offerings and drink offerings as prescribed, an offering to the Lord as a pleasing aroma.
On the tenth day of this seventh month, you shall have a holy assembly, and you shall do no ordinary work.
Present whole burnt offerings to the Lord as a pleasing aroma: one young bull, one ram, and seven year-old lambs, without defect.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of a measure for the bull and two tenths of a measure for the ram.
And one tenth of a measure for each lamb, for all seven lambs.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the burnt offering of atonement and the regular whole burnt offering, with their grain offerings and drink offerings.
On the fifteenth day of this seventh month, you shall have a holy assembly, and you shall do no ordinary work. Celebrate a festival to the Lord for seven days.
Present a whole burnt offering, an offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord: thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs, without defect.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of a measure for each bull, for all thirteen bulls, and two tenths of a measure for each ram, for both rams.
And one tenth of a measure for each lamb, for all fourteen lambs.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular whole burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
On the second day: twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs, without defect.
And the grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to their number, as prescribed.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular whole burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
On the third day: eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs, without defect.
And the grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to their number, as prescribed.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular whole burnt offering, its fine-flour offering, and its drink offering.
On the fourth day: ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs, without defect.
And the grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to their number, as prescribed.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular whole burnt offering with its fine flour offering and its drink offering.
And on the fifth day, nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs without blemish.
And their fine flour offerings and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed for them.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular whole burnt offering with its fine flour offering and its drink offering.
On the sixth day, eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs without blemish.
And their fine flour offerings and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed for them.
And one male goat for sin, besides the regular whole burnt offering with its fine flour offering and its drink offering.
And on the seventh day, seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs without blemish.
And their fine flour offerings and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed for them.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular whole burnt offering with its fine flour offering and its drink offering.
And on the eighth day you shall gather together, and you shall do no ordinary work.
And offer whole burnt offerings, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord: one young bull, one ram, and four year-old lambs without blemish.
And their fine flour offerings and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed for them.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular whole burnt offering with its fine flour offering and its drink offering.

You shall offer these to the Lord at the times of your festivals, besides your vows and besides your voluntary offerings, your whole burnt offerings, your fine flour offerings, your drink offerings, and your sacrifices.
And Moses told the Israelites everything that the Lord had commanded Moses.
And Moses spoke with the heads of the tribes of the Israelites and said to them, “This is what the Lord has commanded:
When a man makes a vow to the Lord, or swears an oath and binds himself to an obligation, he shall not break his word. He shall do everything that has come from his mouth.
And when a woman makes a vow to the Lord and binds herself to an obligation while she is young and in her father's house,
and her father hears the vows and obligations to which she has bound herself, and her father says nothing to her, all the vows and all the obligations to which she has bound herself shall stand.
But if her father annuls them on the day he hears of them, none of the vows or obligations to which she has bound herself shall stand. And the Lord will forgive her, because her father annulled them.
And if she marries while under her vows or a pledge spoken by her lips by which she has bound herself,
and her husband hears of it and says nothing to her on the day he hears, all her vows shall stand, and the obligations to which she has bound herself shall stand.
But if her husband annuls them on the day he hears, the vows and the pledges spoken by her lips by which she has bound herself shall be annulled, and the Lord will forgive her.
And as for the vow of a widow or a divorced woman, everything to which she binds herself shall remain binding on her.
If she made a vow in her husband's house, or bound herself by an obligation under oath,
And if her husband hears and says nothing to her and does not annul them, all her vows shall stand, and all the obligations to which she has bound herself shall stand.

and her husband explicitly cancels them on the day he hears about them, nothing that came from her lips concerning her vows or the obligations she imposed on herself shall stand, because her husband canceled them. The Lord will forgive her.
Her husband may confirm or cancel all her vows and all her binding oaths to deny herself.

But if her husband remains silent toward her from day to day, all her vows and all the obligations she has imposed on herself will stand, because her husband remained silent toward her on the day he heard them.
But if he cancels them after he has heard them, he will bear her guilt.
These are the laws that the Lord commanded Moses concerning a husband and his wife, and a father and his daughter while she is young and living in her father’s house.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites, and afterward you will be gathered to your people.”
Moses said to the people, “Arm men from among you for the army, so that they may go against the Midianites and carry out the Lord’s vengeance on the Midianites.
Send a thousand from each tribe, from all the tribes of the Israelites, into the army.”
So a thousand from each tribe were chosen from the thousands of Israel: twelve thousand men armed for the army.

Moses sent them into the army, a thousand from each tribe, twelve thousand armed men, along with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, who carried the sacred utensils and the trumpets for sounding the alarm.
They fought against Midian as the Lord had commanded Moses, and they killed every male.
Along with the others they killed, they killed the kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five Midianite kings. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
The Israelites took the women of Midian and their children captive, and plundered all their livestock, all their possessions, and all their property.
They burned all the towns where they lived and all their encampments.
They carried away all the captives and all the plunder, both people and livestock.
They brought the captives, the plunder, and the spoils to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the whole assembly of the Israelites, to the camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the assembly went outside the camp to meet them.
Moses was angry with the army officers, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, who had returned from the military campaign.
Moses said to them, “Why have you kept all the females alive?”

“These women were a stumbling block to the Israelites through Balaam’s advice, and they rebelled and acted unfaithfully against the Lord in the affair of Peor, so that a sudden plague struck the Lord’s assembly.
Now kill all the boys, and kill every woman who has slept with a man.
But keep alive for yourselves all the young girls who have not slept with a man.
As for you, camp outside the camp for seven days. Sprinkle everyone who has killed a person or touched someone who was killed on the third day and on the seventh day, both you and your captives.
Sprinkle every garment, every leather article, everything made of hair, and every wooden article.”
Eleazar the priest said to the soldiers who had returned from battle, “This is the requirement of the law that the Lord commanded Moses:
“However, gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead—
Everything that goes into the furnace, pass through fire, and it will be clean. Sprinkle the water of purification on it. Everything that does not pass through fire, immerse in water.
Wash your clothes on the seventh day, and you will be clean. After that, you may enter the camp.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
You, Eleazar the priest, and the heads of the ancestral families of the congregation must count the plunder and the captives, both people and livestock.
Divide the plunder between the fighting men who went out with the army and the whole congregation.
Set aside a levy for the Lord from the fighting men who went out with the army and from the whole congregation: one in fifty of the people, cattle, donkeys, and sheep.
Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the Lord’s contribution.
From the Israelites’ half, take one in fifty of the people, donkeys, cattle, sheep, and all the livestock. Give them to the Levites who perform the duties of the Lord’s tabernacle.
Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The plunder and captives that the people and the army had taken amounted to 675,000 sheep,
72,000 cattle,
61,000 donkeys,
and 32,000 people in all, consisting of women who had never slept with a male.
The half allotted to those who had gone out with the army amounted to 337,500 sheep.
The levy for the Lord from the sheep was 6,750.
There were 36,000 cattle, and their levy for the Lord was 720.
There were 30,500 donkeys, and their levy for the Lord was 610.
There were 16,000 people, and their levy for the Lord was 320 people.
Moses gave the silver of the Lord’s contribution to Eleazar the priest, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
From the Israelites’ half, which Moses had allotted to them from the men who had gone out with the army.
The congregation's half of the flock amounted to three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred.
And 36,000 cattle,
30,500 donkeys,
and 16,000 people.
Moses took one in fifty of the people and livestock from the Israelites’ half and gave them to the Levites who performed the duties of the Lord’s tabernacle, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The men appointed over the army’s thousands—the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds—approached Moses.
They said to Moses, “Your servants have counted the fighting men under our command, and not one man is missing.
We have brought an offering to the Lord, each man bringing the gold ornaments he found: anklets, bracelets, rings, earrings, and necklaces, to make atonement for ourselves before the Lord.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, all of it crafted objects.
All the gold of the contribution that they set apart for the Lord, from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, amounted to sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty shekels.
But the soldiers had taken plunder, each for himself.

Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the Lord.
The descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad had very large herds of livestock. They saw that Jazer and the land of Gilead were suitable places for livestock.
The descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad came and spoke to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the assembly:
“Ataroth, Ribon [?], Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sheba, Nebo, and Beon—
the land that the Lord devastated before the Israelites—is land suitable for livestock, and your servants have livestock.”
They said, “If we have found favor with you, let this land be given to your servants as an inheritance. Do not make us cross the Jordan.”
Moses said to the descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad, “Are your brothers to go to war while you stay here?
Why are you discouraging the Israelites from crossing into the land that the Lord has given them?
This is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to explore the land.
They went up as far as the Valley of the Grape Cluster and saw the land. They discouraged the Israelites from entering the land that the Lord had given them.
The Lord's anger burned against them that day, and he swore, saying:
‘The men who came up from Egypt, twenty years old and older, shall not see the land that I swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they did not follow me wholeheartedly,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, who followed the Lord wholeheartedly.’
The Lord’s anger burned against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the entire generation of men who had done evil before the Lord had perished.
And now you too have risen up today in your fathers’ place, a brood of sinful men, to increase the Lord’s anger against Israel still further.
If you turn away from the Lord, he will again make you wander in the wilderness, and you will bring destruction on this whole people.”
They approached him and said, “We will build sheepfolds here for our livestock and towns for our families.

But we ourselves will arm ourselves and go ahead of the Israelites until we have brought them to their place. Our families will stay in fortified towns for protection from the inhabitants of the land.
We will not return to our homes until every Israelite has received his inheritance.
We will not receive an inheritance with them on the other side of the Jordan and beyond, because we have received our inheritance on the eastern side of the Jordan.”
Moses said to them, “If you do this and arm yourselves for battle before the Lord,
and all of you cross the Jordan armed for battle before the Lord, until he has destroyed his enemies before him,
and the land is subdued before the Lord, then you may return and be free of obligation to the Lord and to Israel. This land will be yours as an inheritance before the Lord.
But if you do not do this, you will be sinning against the Lord. Know that your sins will catch up with you.
Build towns for your families and pens for your flocks, and do what you have promised.
The descendants of Reuben and Gad said to Moses, “Your servants will do as our lord commands.
Our families, our wives, our possessions, and all our livestock will remain in the towns of Gilead.”
Your servants will cross over, armed for battle, before the Lord, as our lord has said.
Moses gave instructions concerning them all to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral tribes of the Israelites.

Moses said to them, “If the descendants of Reuben and Gad cross the Jordan with you, armed for battle before the Lord, and the land is subdued before you, give them the land of Gilead as their inheritance.
But if they do not cross over with you armed, they will receive their inheritance among you in the land of Canaan.”
The descendants of Reuben and Gad answered Moses, “We will do just as the Lord has told your servants.
We will cross over, armed for battle before the Lord, into the land of Canaan, but our inherited property will be on this side of the Jordan.”

Moses gave the descendants of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan—the whole land and its towns within its borders, and the towns of the surrounding land.
The descendants of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, and Aroer,
Atroth-shophan, Jazer, and Jogbehah,
Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran—fortified towns—and pens for the flocks.
The descendants of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kiriathaim.
And Nebo and Baal-meon, whose names had been changed, and Sibmah. They gave names to the towns they built.
The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, conquered it, and destroyed the Amorites who were there.
Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their villages and named them the Villages of Jair, as they are called to this day.
Nobah went and captured Kenath [?] and its villages, and named it Nobah after himself.
These are the stages of the journey of the Israelites, who came out of the land of Egypt in their divisions under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
Moses recorded their departures and the stages of their journey at the Lord’s command. These are the stages of their journey and their departures.
They set out from Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month. After the Passover, the Israelites left Egypt with a raised hand, in full view of all the Egyptians.
The Egyptians were burying the firstborn whom the Lord had killed among them. The Lord also carried out judgment against their gods.
The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
They set out from Etham and camped at Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon, and camped in front of Migdol.
They set out from Pi-hahiroth and passed through the sea into the wilderness. They traveled for three days in the wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.
They set out from Marah and came to Elim. At Elim there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there beside the water.
They set out from Elim and camped beside the Red Sea.
They set out from beside the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim. There was no water there for the people to drink.
They set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They set out from Ekrona and camped at Ezion-geber.
They set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Zin, which is Kadesh.
They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom.
Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor at the LORD’s command and died there, in the fortieth year after the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt, on the first day of the first month.
Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite king of Geder, who lived in the south in the land of Canaan, heard when the Israelites came.
They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
They set out from Iye-abarim and camped at Ribon-gad.
They set out from Ribon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped at Mount Abarim, opposite Nebo.
They set out from Mount Abarim and camped in the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan at Jericho.
They camped beside the Jordan, from Beth-jeshimon as far as Abel-shittim, in the plains of Moab.
The Lord spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan across from Jericho.
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: You are crossing the Jordan into the land of Canaan.
You must destroy all the inhabitants of the land before you. You must destroy all their objects of worship and all their cast images, and demolish all their high places.
You will take possession of the land and settle in it, because I have given you the land to possess.

Take possession of the land by lot according to your clans. Give a larger inheritance to the larger groups and a smaller inheritance to the smaller groups. Whoever receives a lot shall inherit according to their ancestral tribes.
But if you do not destroy the inhabitants of the land before you, those who remain will become spikes in your eyes and thorns in your temples, and they will trouble you in the land where you live.
And I will do to you what I intended to do to them.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
Command the Israelites and tell them: You are entering the land of Canaan. This is the land that will be allotted to you as an inheritance—the land of Canaan within its borders.
Your southern side will extend from the wilderness of Zin along the border of Edom. Your southern boundary will begin at the eastern end of the Salt Sea.
Your boundary will turn south toward the ascent of Sepharvaim and pass on to Zin. It will extend south of Rekem-geya, go out to Hazar-addar, and pass on to Azmon.
The boundary shall turn from Azmon to the Wadi of Egypt, and it shall end at the sea.
Your western boundary shall be the Great Sea and its coastline. This shall be your western boundary.
This shall be your northern boundary: from the Great Sea you shall mark out a boundary to Mount Hor.
From Mount Hor you shall mark out a boundary to the entrance of Hamath, and the boundary shall extend to Zedad.
The boundary shall continue to Ziphron and end at Hazar-enan. These shall be your northern boundaries.
You shall mark out your eastern boundary from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
The boundary shall go down from Shepham to Diblath, east of Ain. The boundary shall go down and reach the eastern shore of the Sea of Chinnereth.
The boundary shall go down to the Jordan and end at the Salt Sea. This shall be your land, with its boundaries all around.
Moses commanded the Israelites and said to them, “This is the land that you shall divide by lot, which the Lord commanded to be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.

For the tribe of Reuben, according to their ancestral households, and the tribe of Gad, according to their ancestral households, have taken their inheritance, and the half-tribe of Manasseh has received its inheritance.
The two tribes and the half-tribe have received their inheritance across the Jordan at Jericho, eastward, there toward the sunrise.”
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
These are the names of the men who will assign the land to you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
Take one leader from each tribe to divide the land among you.
“These are the names of the leaders of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh.
From the tribe of Simeon, Shelumiel son of Ammihud.
From the tribe of Benjamin, Eldad son of Chislon.
From the tribe of Dan, Bukki son of Jogli.
From the tribe of Joseph, from the tribe of Manasseh, Nahaliel son of Ephod.
From the tribe of Ephraim, Kemuel son of Shiphtan.
From the tribe of Zebulun, Elizaphan son of Parnach.
From the tribe of Issachar, Paltiel son of Azzan.
From the tribe of Asher, Ahihud son of Shelomi.
From the tribe of Naphtali, Pedahel son of Ammihud.”
These are the men whom the Lord commanded to assign the Israelites their inheritance in the land of Canaan.
The Lord spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho and said to him:
“Command the Israelites to give the Levites towns to live in from their inherited holdings. They shall also give the Levites the pasturelands surrounding the towns.
The towns shall be theirs to live in, and their pasturelands shall be for their livestock, their possessions, and all their animals.
The pasturelands of the towns that you give to the Levites shall extend a thousand cubits outward from the town wall, all around.

Measure outside the town two thousand cubits on the east side, two thousand cubits on the south side, two thousand cubits on the west side, and two thousand cubits on the north side, with the town in the middle. This shall be the open land belonging to your towns.

Among the towns you give to the Levites, six towns shall be cities of refuge for you, so that a killer who has killed his neighbor unintentionally may flee there. In addition to these, give forty-two towns.
All the towns you give to the Levites shall be forty-eight towns, together with their open lands.

As for the towns you give from the Israelites' inheritance, give more from those who have much and fewer from those who have little. Each shall give some of his towns to the Levites in proportion to the inheritance he receives.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
prepare towns for yourselves to serve as cities of refuge, so that a killer, someone who kills a person accidentally, may flee there.
These towns shall be a refuge for you from the avenger of blood, so that the killer will not be put to death before standing trial before the assembly.
The towns you give shall be six cities of refuge for you.
Give three towns beyond the Jordan, and give three towns in the land of Canaan. They shall be cities of refuge.
For the Israelites, for anyone who turns to me, and for those who live among you, these six towns shall be a refuge, so that anyone who kills a person accidentally may flee to them.
If someone strikes another person with an iron implement in a way that could kill him, and he dies, he is a murderer. That murderer must be put to death.
If someone strikes another person with a stone held in his hand in a way that could kill him, and he dies, he is a murderer. He must be put to death.
If someone strikes another person with a wooden implement held in his hand in a way that could kill him, and he dies, he is a murderer. He must be put to death.
The avenger of blood himself shall kill the murderer when he encounters him.
If he struck him out of hatred, or threw something at him deliberately, and he died, he is a murderer.
If he struck him with his hand out of hostility, intending to kill him, and he died, he is a murderer and must be put to death. The avenger of blood shall kill the murderer when he encounters him.
But if someone suddenly strikes another person without hostility, or throws any implement at him without malicious intent,
or throws any deadly stone onto him without seeing him, and he dies, though he was not his enemy and did not wish him harm,
the assembly shall judge between the killer and the avenger of blood according to these rulings.

The congregation shall rescue the killer from the avenger of blood, and the congregation shall send him back to the city of refuge to which he had fled. He shall live there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the killer goes outside the boundaries of the city of refuge to which he fled,
and the avenger of blood finds him outside the boundaries of the city of refuge, and the avenger of blood kills the killer, he bears no bloodguilt.
For this reason, he must live in the city of refuge until the high priest dies. When the high priest dies, the killer may return to the land of his inheritance.
These laws shall remain in force for you forever, throughout your generations, wherever you live.
Whenever anyone kills a person, the killer shall be put to death on the testimony of witnesses. But a single witness must not testify against someone to have him put to death.
Do not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves death. He must be put to death.
Do not accept a ransom for someone to flee to a city of refuge and then go and live in the land until the high priest dies.
Do not pollute the land in which you live, for blood pollutes the land. No atonement can be made for the land in which blood has been shed unless the blood of the one who shed it is shed there.
Do not defile the land in which you live, where I dwell, for I am the Lord, who dwells among the Israelites.

The heads of the ancestral families of the clan of the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the clan of Manasseh son of Joseph, came forward. They spoke before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, and before the leaders of the congregation, the heads of the ancestral families of the Israelites.

They said, “The Lord commanded our lord to give the land to the Israelites as an inheritance by lot. Our lord was also commanded by the Lord to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

But if they marry men from another of the tribes of the Israelites, their inheritance will be taken away from their fathers’ inheritance and added to the inheritance of the tribes into which they marry. It will be taken away from our allotted inheritance.

And when the Jubilee comes for the Israelites, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribes into which they marry, and their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of their fathers’ tribe.”
Moses gave the Israelites a command according to the word spoken by the Lord, saying, “The tribe of the descendants of Joseph is right in what it says.
This is what the Lord has commanded concerning Zelophehad’s daughters: They may marry whomever they please, but they must marry within the tribe of their father’s clan.
The inheritance of the Israelites must not pass from one tribe to another. Rather, the Israelites must each hold on to the inheritance of their ancestral tribe.
Every daughter who inherits property in any of the tribes of the Israelites must marry someone from the clan of her father’s tribe, so that each Israelite may inherit the property of his ancestors.
No inheritance must pass from one tribe to another. Rather, the tribes of the Israelites must each hold on to their own inheritance.”
Zelophehad’s daughters did just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and [?], the daughters of Zelophehad, married the sons of their paternal uncles.
They married within the clan of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of their father’s clan.
These are the commandments, laws, and judgments that the Lord commanded the Israelites through Moses in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.
